Each Party irrevocably and unconditionally waives any objection to the laying of venue of any Action arising out of or relating to this Agreement in any such court, and irrevocably and unconditionally waives and agrees not to plead or claim in any such court that any such Action has been brought in an inconvenient forum. Each Party irrevocably consents to service of process in the manner provided for notices in Section 10.01; *provided* that nothing herein shall affect the right of any Party to serve process in any other manner permitted by applicable Law.
**Section 10.04 Waiver of Jury Trial**

**EACH PARTY HEREBY IRREVOCABLY AND UNCONDITIONALLY WAIVES, TO THE FULLEST EXTENT PERMITTED BY APPLICABLE LAW, ANY AND ALL RIGHT TO TRIAL BY JURY IN ANY ACTION ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT OR THE TRANSACTIONS CONTEMPLATED HEREBY. EACH PARTY CERTIFIES AND ACKNOWLEDGES THAT (A) NO REPRESENTATIVE OF ANY OTHER PARTY HAS REPRESENTED, EXPRESSLY OR OTHERWISE, THAT SUCH OTHER PARTY WOULD NOT, IN THE EVENT OF ANY SUCH ACTION, SEEK TO ENFORCE THE FOREGOING WAIVER, (B) EACH PARTY UNDERSTANDS AND HAS CONSIDERED THE IMPLICATIONS OF THIS WAIVER, (C) EACH PARTY MAKES THIS WAIVER VOLUNTARILY, AND (D) EACH PARTY HAS BEEN INDUCED TO ENTER INTO THIS AGREEMENT BY, AMONG OTHER THINGS, THE MUTUAL WAIVERS AND CERTIFICATIONS IN THIS SECTION 10.04.**

123: \"**Indebtedness**\" means, with respect to any Person, without duplication, (a) all obligations for borrowed money, (b) all obligations evidenced by bonds, debentures, notes, or similar instruments, (c) all obligations under capital leases or financing leases (as determined in accordance with GAAP), (d) all obligations for the deferred purchase price of property or services (other than trade payables incurred in the ordinary course of business), (e) all obligations, contingent or otherwise, under letters of credit (including standby and commercial), to the extent drawn upon, (f) all guarantees of any of the foregoing obligations of another Person, (g) all net obligations under interest rate swap, cap, collar, or similar agreements, and (h) all accrued and unpaid interest, premiums, penalties, fees, expenses, and other amounts payable in connection with the prepayment or repayment of any of the foregoing, including breakage costs. 131: \"**Losses**\" means any and all losses, damages, liabilities, deficiencies, judgments, interest, awards, penalties, fines, costs, and expenses (including reasonable and documented out-of-pocket attorneys\' fees, costs of investigation, and costs of enforcement of indemnification rights), but expressly excluding punitive damages (except to the extent awarded to a third party in a Third-Party Claim), consequential damages, and lost profits.

133: \"**Material Adverse Effect**\" means any event, change, effect, development, state of facts, condition, circumstance, or occurrence that, individually or in the aggregate, has had or would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on (a) the business, assets, liabilities, financial condition, or results of operations of the Company, or (b) the ability of Seller to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement; *provided*, *however*, that none of the following, individually or in the aggregate, shall be deemed to constitute, or shall be taken into account in determining whether there has been or would reasonably be expected to be, a Material Adverse Effect:
134: 
135: > \(i\) changes in general economic, financial, credit, securities market, or political conditions in the United States or globally;

138: >

140: >

142: >
143: > \(v\) acts of war (whether or not declared), armed hostilities, sabotage, terrorism, military actions, or any escalation or worsening thereof, epidemics, pandemics, earthquakes, hurricanes, tornados, floods, or other natural disasters or acts of God;
144: >
145: > \(vi\) the announcement or pendency of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, including any impact on relationships with customers, suppliers, employees, or Governmental Authorities;

153: \"**Net Working Capital**\" or \"**NWC**\" means, as of any date of determination, the current assets of the Company minus the current liabilities of the Company, in each case as determined in accordance with the Accounting Principles and the illustrative NWC calculation set forth on Exhibit C, and excluding (a) cash and cash equivalents, (b) the current portion of any Indebtedness, (c) the current portion of any Transaction Expenses, and (d) deferred tax assets and deferred tax liabilities.
154: 
155: \"**Outside Date**\" means February 28, 2026.
156: 
157: \"**Party**\" and \"**Parties**\" have the meanings set forth in the preamble.
158: 
159: \"**Permits**\" means all licenses, permits, franchises, authorizations, approvals, registrations, consents, certificates, variances, and similar rights obtained from any Governmental Authority.
160: 
161: \"**Permitted Encumbrances**\" means (a) liens for Taxes not yet due and payable or that are being contested in good faith by appropriate proceedings and for which adequate reserves have been established in accordance with GAAP, (b) mechanics\', carriers\', workmen\'s, repairmen\'s, or other similar liens arising in the ordinary course of business securing obligations that are not overdue, (c) easements, rights-of-way, covenants, conditions, restrictions, and other similar encumbrances of record that do not, individually or in the aggregate, materially interfere with the current use or operation of the properties to which they relate, (d) zoning, building codes, and other land use regulations imposed by any Governmental Authority, (e) liens securing the Indebtedness described in the definition of \"Indebtedness\" (which shall be released at or prior to the Closing), and (f) other imperfections of title or encumbrances that do not, individually or in the aggregate, materially impair the continued use and operation of the assets to which they relate in the conduct of the business of the Company as currently conducted.
162: 
163: \"**Person**\" means any individual, corporation, partnership, joint venture, limited liability company, association, trust, unincorporated organization, Governmental Authority, or other entity.
164: 
165: \"**Purchase Price**\" has the meaning set forth in Section 2.02.
166: 
167: \"**Release**\" means any release, spill, emission, discharge, leaking, pumping, pouring, dumping, injection, deposit, disposal, dispersal, leaching, or migration into or through the environment (including ambient air, surface water, groundwater, land surface, or subsurface strata) or into or out of any property, including the movement of Hazardous Substances through or in the air, soil, surface water, groundwater, or property.
168: 
169: \"**Representative**\" means, with respect to any Person, such Person\'s directors, officers, employees, managers, members, partners, equityholders, agents, advisors (including financial advisors, attorneys, and accountants), and other representatives.
170: 
171: \"**Seller**\" has the meaning set forth in the preamble.
172: 
173: \"**Seller Indemnitees**\" has the meaning set forth in Section 9.03.
174: 
175: \"**Shares**\" has the meaning set forth in the Recitals.
176: 
177: \"**Target NWC**\" means Eighteen Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$18,200,000).
178: 
179: \"**Tax**\" or \"**Taxes**\" means any and all federal, state, local, or non-U.S. income, gross receipts, license, payroll, employment, excise, severance, stamp, occupation, premium, windfall profits, environmental, customs duties, capital stock, franchise, profits, withholding, social security (or similar), unemployment, disability, real property, personal property, sales, use, transfer, registration, value-added, alternative or add-on minimum, estimated, or other tax of any kind whatsoever, including any interest, penalty, or addition thereto, whether disputed or not, and any obligations under any agreements or arrangements with any other Person with respect to such amounts and any liability for such amounts as a result of being a member of an affiliated, consolidated, combined, or unitary group for any period.
180: 
181: \"**Tax Return**\" means any return, declaration, report, claim for refund, information return or statement, or other document relating to Taxes, including any schedule or attachment thereto, and including any amendment thereof.
182: 
183: \"**Transaction Documents**\" means this Agreement, the Escrow Agreement, and each other agreement, instrument, certificate, or document executed or delivered in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement.
184: 
185: \"**Transaction Expenses**\" means all fees, costs, expenses, and other amounts incurred by or on behalf of Seller or the Company (whether or not paid) in connection with the negotiation, preparation, execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement and the Transaction Documents and the consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby and thereby, including (a) all legal, accounting, tax advisory, financial advisory, consulting, and other professional fees and expenses, (b) all fees, expenses, premiums, and other amounts payable to any broker, finder, investment banker, or similar intermediary, (c) all change-of-control, transaction, retention, stay, or similar bonuses or payments payable to any employee, officer, director, or consultant of the Company in connection with or as a result of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, and (d) the employer\'s share of any payroll, social security, unemployment, or similar Taxes attributable to any of the foregoing amounts.
186: 
187: **Section 1.02 Interpretation**
188: 
189: Unless the context of this Agreement otherwise requires: (a) words of one gender include the other genders; (b) words using the singular or plural number also include the plural or singular number, respectively; (c) the terms \"hereof,\" \"herein,\" \"hereby,\" \"hereto,\" and derivative or similar words refer to this entire Agreement; (d) the terms \"Article,\" \"Section,\" \"Schedule,\" \"Exhibit,\" and \"Recital\" refer to the specified Article, Section, Schedule, Exhibit, or Recital of or to this Agreement, unless otherwise specified; (e) the word \"including\" and words of similar import shall mean \"including, without limitation,\" unless otherwise specified; (f) the word \"or\" is not exclusive; (g) all references to \"\$\" or \"dollars\" mean the lawful currency of the United States of America; (h) the word \"extent\" in the phrase \"to the extent\" shall mean the degree to which a subject or other thing extends, and such phrase shall not mean simply \"if\"; (i) references to a statute or regulation mean such statute or regulation as amended, modified, supplemented, or replaced from time to time (and, in the case of any statute, include any rules and regulations promulgated under such statute) and references to any section of any statute or regulation include any successor to such section; (j) all references to any period of days shall mean the relevant number of calendar days unless otherwise specified; (k) if the last day for giving any notice or taking any action under this Agreement is a day that is not a Business Day, then the time for giving such notice or taking such action shall be extended to the next succeeding Business Day; (l) headings of Articles and Sections are for convenience of reference only and do not affect the interpretation of this Agreement; and (m) all Exhibits and Schedules annexed hereto or referred to herein are hereby incorporated in and made a part of this Agreement as if set forth herein in full.

191: **[ARTICLE II]{.underline}**
192: 
193: **[PURCHASE AND SALE; PURCHASE PRICE]{.underline}**
194: 
195: **Section 2.01 Purchase and Sale of Shares**
196: 
197: Upon the terms and subject to the conditions of this Agreement, at the Closing, Seller shall sell, assign, transfer, convey, and deliver to Buyer, and Buyer shall purchase, acquire, and accept from Seller, all of the Shares, constituting 1,000,000 shares of common stock, par value \$0.01 per share, of the Company, which represent all of the issued and outstanding shares of capital stock of the Company, free and clear of all Encumbrances (other than restrictions arising under applicable securities Laws), for the Purchase Price, payable as provided in Sections 2.02 and 2.03.
198: 
199: **Section 2.02 Purchase Price**
200: 
201: The aggregate purchase price for the Shares (the \"Purchase Price\") shall be an amount equal to (a) the Base Enterprise Value (\$215,000,000), *plus* (b) the amount, if any, by which the Estimated Closing NWC exceeds the Target NWC, *minus* (c) the amount, if any, by which the Target NWC exceeds the Estimated Closing NWC, *minus* (d) the Estimated Closing Indebtedness, *minus* (e) the Estimated Transaction Expenses. For illustrative purposes only, based on preliminary estimates, the Purchase Price would be calculated as follows: \$215,000,000 + \$18,200,000 (Estimated Closing NWC at Target) -- \$42,300,000 (Estimated Closing Indebtedness) -- \$3,900,000 (Estimated Transaction Expenses) = \$187,000,000. The Purchase Price shall be subject to adjustment as provided in Sections 2.03 and 2.04. The Purchase Price does not include any Earnout Payment that may become payable pursuant to Section 2.05, which shall be in addition to the Purchase Price.
202: 
203: **Section 2.03 Closing Payment and Estimates**
204: 
205: **(a)** *Pre-Closing Estimate.* Not later than three (3) Business Days prior to the Closing Date, Seller shall prepare and deliver to Buyer a written statement (the \"Estimated Closing Statement\") setting forth Seller\'s good-faith estimates of: (i) the Closing NWC (the \"Estimated Closing NWC\"), (ii) the Closing Indebtedness (the \"Estimated Closing Indebtedness\"), and (iii) the Transaction Expenses (the \"Estimated Transaction Expenses\"), together with reasonable supporting documentation, schedules, and work papers used in the preparation thereof. The Estimated Closing Statement shall be prepared in accordance with the Accounting Principles and shall include a calculation of the estimated Purchase Price based on such estimates. Seller shall provide Buyer with reasonable access to the books and records of the Company and the work papers of the Company\'s accountants as Buyer may reasonably request to verify the Estimated Closing Statement. If Buyer delivers written notice of any objections to the Estimated Closing Statement within two (2) Business Days after receipt thereof, the Parties shall negotiate in good faith to resolve such objections prior to the Closing Date; *provided* that the failure of the Parties to resolve any such objections shall not delay the Closing, and the Estimated Closing Statement, as adjusted by mutual agreement of the Parties (or, absent such agreement, as originally delivered by Seller), shall be used for purposes of calculating the Closing Payment, subject to the post-Closing adjustment procedures set forth in Section 2.04.
206: 
207: **(b)** *Closing Payment.* At the Closing, Buyer shall pay to Seller an aggregate amount in cash (the \"Closing Payment\") equal to (i) the Purchase Price (calculated using the estimates set forth in the Estimated Closing Statement), *minus* (ii) the Escrow Amount (\$16,125,000). The Closing Payment shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds to one or more bank accounts designated in writing by Seller to Buyer no later than two (2) Business Days prior to the Closing Date.
208: 
209: **(c)** *Escrow Deposit.* At the Closing, Buyer shall deposit the Escrow Amount, in cash, by wire transfer of immediately available funds, with the Escrow Agent in accordance with the terms of the Escrow Agreement. The Escrow Fund shall be held, invested, and disbursed by the Escrow Agent in accordance with the terms of the Escrow Agreement. The Escrow Fund shall serve as security for Seller\'s indemnification obligations under Article IX and the post-Closing adjustment obligations under Section 2.04, as and to the extent provided herein and in the Escrow Agreement.
210: 
211: **(d)** *Repayment of Closing Indebtedness.* At or promptly following the Closing, Buyer shall cause the Company to repay, discharge, and satisfy in full all Closing Indebtedness. Seller shall use commercially reasonable efforts to cooperate with Buyer in connection with the repayment of such Closing Indebtedness.
212: 
213: **Section 2.04 Post-Closing NWC Adjustment**
214: 
215: **(a)** *Closing Statement.* Within ninety (90) days following the Closing Date, Buyer shall prepare and deliver to Seller a written statement (the \"Closing Statement\") setting forth Buyer\'s good-faith calculation of the actual (i) Closing NWC, (ii) Closing Indebtedness, and (iii) Transaction Expenses, together with reasonable supporting documentation, schedules, and work papers. The Closing Statement shall be prepared in accordance with the Accounting Principles and in a manner consistent with the preparation of the Estimated Closing Statement. Buyer shall provide Seller and its Representatives with reasonable access, during normal business hours and upon reasonable prior notice, to the books and records of the Company and the work papers used in the preparation of the Closing Statement.
216: 
217: **(b)** *Review and Objection.* Seller shall have thirty (30) days following receipt of the Closing Statement (the \"Review Period\") to review the Closing Statement. During the Review Period, Buyer shall provide Seller and its Representatives with reasonable access to the books and records of the Company, the work papers of the Company\'s accountants, and the personnel of the Company, in each case to the extent reasonably necessary for Seller\'s review of the Closing Statement. If Seller does not deliver a written notice of objection (an \"Objection Notice\") to Buyer within the Review Period, the Closing Statement as delivered by Buyer shall be deemed final and binding on the Parties. If Seller delivers an Objection Notice within the Review Period, such Objection Notice shall specify in reasonable detail each item in dispute (each, a \"Disputed Item\"), the basis for such dispute, and the amount Seller believes to be the correct amount. Any item or amount not specifically identified as a Disputed Item in the Objection Notice shall be deemed accepted by Seller and shall be final and binding on the Parties.
218: 
219: **(c)** *Resolution of Disputes.* If Seller delivers a timely Objection Notice, the Parties shall negotiate in good faith for a period of twenty (20) Business Days following delivery of the Objection Notice (the \"Resolution Period\") to resolve all Disputed Items. If the Parties are unable to resolve all Disputed Items within the Resolution Period, any remaining Disputed Items shall be submitted for final resolution to an independent, nationally recognized accounting firm mutually agreed upon by Buyer and Seller (the \"Independent Accountant\"); *provided* that such firm shall not be Winslow & Tate CPA Group, the auditors of the Company, or any accounting firm that has provided services to Buyer or Seller during the twenty-four (24) month period prior to such engagement. The Independent Accountant shall be engaged to resolve only the remaining Disputed Items and shall determine the correct amount of each such Disputed Item in accordance with the Accounting Principles, and such determination shall be final and binding on the Parties, absent manifest error. The Independent Accountant shall not assign a value to any Disputed Item that is greater than the highest value or less than the lowest value claimed by either Party. The Independent Accountant shall render its written determination within thirty (30) days after such engagement and shall set forth in such determination a reasoned basis for its resolution of each Disputed Item. The fees and expenses of the Independent Accountant shall be allocated between the Parties based on the relative amounts of the aggregate Disputed Items resolved in favor of each Party (as determined by the Independent Accountant), such that the Party whose positions are furthest from the Independent Accountant\'s determinations bears a proportionally greater share of such fees and expenses.
220: 
221: **(d)** *Adjustment Payment.* Within five (5) Business Days after the final determination of the Closing Statement (as determined pursuant to this Section 2.04):
222: 
223: > \(i\) If the Purchase Price as finally determined (using the actual Closing NWC, Closing Indebtedness, and Transaction Expenses as finally determined) exceeds the Purchase Price as calculated using the Estimated Closing Statement, Buyer shall pay such excess amount to Seller by wire transfer of immediately available funds.
224: >
225: > \(ii\) If the Purchase Price as calculated using the Estimated Closing Statement exceeds the Purchase Price as finally determined, Seller shall pay such excess amount to Buyer (first, by instructing the Escrow Agent to release such amount from the Escrow Fund, and, to the extent the Escrow Fund is insufficient, by wire transfer of immediately available funds from Seller directly to Buyer).
226: 
227: All adjustments pursuant to this Section 2.04 shall be made on a dollar-for-dollar basis from the first dollar of any difference, without any collar, threshold, or de minimis amount. Any adjustment amounts payable under this Section 2.04 shall bear interest from the Closing Date through the date of payment at the prime rate as published in *The Wall Street Journal* on the Closing Date (or, if the Closing Date is not a Business Day, on the immediately preceding Business Day), calculated on the basis of a 365-day year and the actual number of days elapsed.
228: 
229: **Section 2.05 Earnout**
230: 
231: **(a)** *Maximum Earnout Payment.* If the Company\'s Adjusted EBITDA for the Earnout Period (the twelve (12) month period ending December 31, 2026) equals or exceeds Thirty-Eight Million Dollars (\$38,000,000), Buyer shall pay to Seller an amount equal to Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000) (the \"Maximum Earnout Payment\").
232: 
233: **(b)** *Pro-Rata Earnout.* If the Company\'s Adjusted EBITDA for the Earnout Period is at least Thirty-Two Million Dollars (\$32,000,000) but less than Thirty-Eight Million Dollars (\$38,000,000), Buyer shall pay to Seller an amount (the \"Earnout Payment\") equal to: (\$25,000,000 ÷ (\$38,000,000 -- \$32,000,000)) × (Actual Adjusted EBITDA -- \$32,000,000). For the avoidance of doubt, this formula results in a linear interpolation, such that the Earnout Payment increases by approximately Four Million One Hundred Sixty-Six Thousand Six Hundred Sixty-Seven Dollars (\$4,166,667) for each One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000) of Adjusted EBITDA in excess of \$32,000,000. If the Company\'s Adjusted EBITDA for the Earnout Period is less than \$32,000,000, no Earnout Payment shall be due or payable.
234: 
235: **(c)** *Earnout Calculation and Dispute Resolution.* Within sixty (60) days after the end of the Earnout Period, Buyer shall prepare and deliver to Seller a written statement (the \"Earnout Statement\") setting forth Buyer\'s good-faith calculation of Adjusted EBITDA for the Earnout Period, together with reasonable supporting documentation. Seller shall have thirty (30) days to review the Earnout Statement and deliver any objections thereto. The dispute resolution procedures set forth in Section 2.04(b) and Section 2.04(c) shall apply *mutatis mutandis* to any dispute with respect to the Earnout Statement.
236: 
237: **(d)** *Operation of the Business During the Earnout Period.* From and after the Closing Date through the end of the Earnout Period, Buyer shall, and shall cause the Company to, operate the business of the Company in a manner consistent with past practice and in good faith to maximize the Earnout Payment. Without limiting the foregoing, Buyer shall not, and shall cause the Company not to, take any action that would reasonably be expected to reduce the Adjusted EBITDA of the Company below the levels that would otherwise have been achieved. In furtherance of the foregoing, during the Earnout Period, Buyer shall cause the Company to maintain substantially the same level of personnel, equipment, and other resources as in effect immediately prior to the Closing Date and shall not divert or redirect any contracts, customers, revenues, or business opportunities of the Company to Buyer or any of its Affiliates. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Buyer acknowledges and agrees that Seller shall have no obligation to contribute resources, personnel, or funds to the Company during the Earnout Period, and the obligations set forth in this Section 2.05(d) are solely obligations of Buyer.
238: 
239: **(e)** *Payment of Earnout.* Any Earnout Payment determined to be payable pursuant to this Section 2.05 shall be paid by Buyer to Seller within ten (10) Business Days after the final determination of Adjusted EBITDA for the Earnout Period (whether by agreement of the Parties, expiration of the review period without objection, or determination of the Independent Accountant), by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account designated by Seller. For U.S. federal income tax purposes, the Parties agree to treat any Earnout Payment as an adjustment to the Purchase Price.
240: 
241: **Section 2.06 Withholding**
242: 
243: Buyer and the Company shall be entitled to deduct and withhold from any amounts payable pursuant to this Agreement such amounts as Buyer, the Company, or the Escrow Agent may be required to deduct and withhold under the Code, or any applicable provision of state, local, or non-U.S. Tax Law, with respect to the making of any such payment. To the extent that amounts are so withheld and remitted to the applicable Governmental Authority, such withheld amounts shall be treated for all purposes of this Agreement as having been paid to the Person in respect of which such deduction and withholding was made.
244: 
245: **Section 2.07 Closing**
246: 
247: The closing of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement (the \"Closing\") shall take place remotely via the electronic exchange of documents and signatures on the date that is three (3) Business Days after the date on which all of the conditions set forth in Article VII have been satisfied or waived (other than those conditions that by their nature are to be satisfied at the Closing, but subject to the satisfaction or waiver of such conditions at the Closing), or at such other time, date, and place as the Parties may mutually agree in writing (the \"Closing Date\"). The Parties anticipate that the Closing will occur in mid-January 2026. The Closing shall be deemed to be effective as of 12:01 a.m. Eastern Time on the Closing Date.
248: 
249: **Section 2.08 Closing Deliverables**
250: 
251: **(a)** *Seller Deliverables.* At the Closing, Seller shall deliver, or cause to be delivered, to Buyer the following:
252: 
253: > \(i\) stock certificates representing all of the Shares, duly endorsed in blank or accompanied by duly executed stock powers, with all required transfer stamps affixed, sufficient to transfer to Buyer good and valid title to all of the Shares, free and clear of all Encumbrances;
254: >
255: > \(ii\) a certificate of good standing (or equivalent certificate) for the Company issued by the Secretary of State of the State of Oregon, and certificates of good standing (or equivalent certificates) for the Company issued by the Secretaries of State of each of the States of Washington, California, and Nevada, in each case dated not more than ten (10) days prior to the Closing Date;
256: >
257: > \(iii\) certified copies of the resolutions duly adopted by the board of directors of Seller authorizing the execution, delivery, and performance by Seller of this Agreement and the Transaction Documents and the consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby and thereby;
258: >
259: > \(iv\) a certificate of non-foreign status of Seller, executed pursuant to Treasury Regulation Section 1.1445-2(b)(2), in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to Buyer (the \"FIRPTA Certificate\");

\"**Indebtedness**\" means, with respect to any Person, without duplication, (a) all obligations for borrowed money, (b) all obligations evidenced by bonds, debentures, notes, or similar instruments, (c) all obligations under capital leases or financing leases (as determined in accordance with GAAP), (d) all obligations for the deferred purchase price of property or services (other than trade payables incurred in the ordinary course of business), (e) all obligations, contingent or otherwise, under letters of credit (including standby and commercial), to the extent drawn upon, (f) all guarantees of any of the foregoing obligations of another Person, (g) all net obligations under interest rate swap, cap, collar, or similar agreements, and (h) all accrued and unpaid interest, premiums, penalties, fees, expenses, and other amounts payable in connection with the prepayment or repayment of any of the foregoing, including breakage costs. Indebtedness of the Company as of the date hereof includes (i) the Twenty-Eight Million Dollar (\$28,000,000) senior term loan with Cascade Mutual Bank, (ii) the Nine Million Eight Hundred Thousand Dollar (\$9,800,000) equipment financing facility with Pacific Lease Corp., and (iii) the Four Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollar (\$4,500,000) subordinated seller note payable to Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc.
\"**Indemnification Cap**\" means Forty-Three Million Dollars (\$43,000,000), which is equal to twenty percent (20%) of the Base Enterprise Value.
\"**Knowledge**\" or \"**Knowledge of the Company**\" means the actual knowledge of Patricia Huang, Chief Executive Officer of the Company, and Robert Merrill, Chief Financial Officer of the Company.

\"**Law**\" means any statute, law, ordinance, regulation, rule, code, executive order, injunction, judgment, decree, directive, or other legally enforceable requirement of any Governmental Authority.

\"**Losses**\" means any and all losses, damages, liabilities, deficiencies, judgments, interest, awards, penalties, fines, costs, and expenses (including reasonable and documented out-of-pocket attorneys\' fees, costs of investigation, and costs of enforcement of indemnification rights), but expressly excluding punitive damages (except to the extent awarded to a third party in a Third-Party Claim), consequential damages, and lost profits.

\"**Material Adverse Effect**\" means any event, change, effect, development, state of facts, condition, circumstance, or occurrence that, individually or in the aggregate, has had or would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on (a) the business, assets, liabilities, financial condition, or results of operations of the Company, or (b) the ability of Seller to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement; *provided*, *however*, that none of the following, individually or in the aggregate, shall be deemed to constitute, or shall be taken into account in determining whether there has been or would reasonably be expected to be, a Material Adverse Effect:
> \(i\) changes in general economic, financial, credit, securities market, or political conditions in the United States or globally;
> \(ii\) changes in conditions generally affecting the environmental services industry;
> \(iii\) changes in Environmental Laws or regulations;
> \(iv\) changes in GAAP or applicable Law (other than Environmental Laws, which are addressed in clause (iii) above);

> \(v\) acts of war (whether or not declared), armed hostilities, sabotage, terrorism, military actions, or any escalation or worsening thereof, epidemics, pandemics, earthquakes, hurricanes, tornados, floods, or other natural disasters or acts of God;
> \(vi\) the announcement or pendency of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, including any impact on relationships with customers, suppliers, employees, or Governmental Authorities;
> \(vii\) any action taken by the Company at the express written request or with the express written consent of Buyer; and

> \(viii\) any failure by the Company to meet any internal or external projections, forecasts, or estimates of revenue, earnings, or other financial performance metrics for any period (provided that the underlying facts, circumstances, and causes of any such failure may be considered in determining whether a Material Adverse Effect has occurred).
\"**Maximum Earnout Payment**\" means Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000).

\"**Net Working Capital**\" or \"**NWC**\" means, as of any date of determination, the current assets of the Company minus the current liabilities of the Company, in each case as determined in accordance with the Accounting Principles and the illustrative NWC calculation set forth on Exhibit C, and excluding (a) cash and cash equivalents, (b) the current portion of any Indebtedness, (c) the current portion of any Transaction Expenses, and (d) deferred tax assets and deferred tax liabilities.
\"**Outside Date**\" means February 28, 2026.
\"**Party**\" and \"**Parties**\" have the meanings set forth in the preamble.
\"**Permits**\" means all licenses, permits, franchises, authorizations, approvals, registrations, consents, certificates, variances, and similar rights obtained from any Governmental Authority.

\"**Permitted Encumbrances**\" means (a) liens for Taxes not yet due and payable or that are being contested in good faith by appropriate proceedings and for which adequate reserves have been established in accordance with GAAP, (b) mechanics\', carriers\', workmen\'s, repairmen\'s, or other similar liens arising in the ordinary course of business securing obligations that are not overdue, (c) easements, rights-of-way, covenants, conditions, restrictions, and other similar encumbrances of record that do not, individually or in the aggregate, materially interfere with the current use or operation of the properties to which they relate, (d) zoning, building codes, and other land use regulations imposed by any Governmental Authority, (e) liens securing the Indebtedness described in the definition of \"Indebtedness\" (which shall be released at or prior to the Closing), and (f) other imperfections of title or encumbrances that do not, individually or in the aggregate, materially impair the continued use and operation of the assets to which they relate in the conduct of the business of the Company as currently conducted.
\"**Person**\" means any individual, corporation, partnership, joint venture, limited liability company, association, trust, unincorporated organization, Governmental Authority, or other entity.
\"**Purchase Price**\" has the meaning set forth in Section 2.02.

\"**Release**\" means any release, spill, emission, discharge, leaking, pumping, pouring, dumping, injection, deposit, disposal, dispersal, leaching, or migration into or through the environment (including ambient air, surface water, groundwater, land surface, or subsurface strata) or into or out of any property, including the movement of Hazardous Substances through or in the air, soil, surface water, groundwater, or property.

\"**Representative**\" means, with respect to any Person, such Person\'s directors, officers, employees, managers, members, partners, equityholders, agents, advisors (including financial advisors, attorneys, and accountants), and other representatives.
\"**Seller**\" has the meaning set forth in the preamble.
\"**Seller Indemnitees**\" has the meaning set forth in Section 9.03.
\"**Shares**\" has the meaning set forth in the Recitals.
\"**Target NWC**\" means Eighteen Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$18,200,000).

\"**Tax**\" or \"**Taxes**\" means any and all federal, state, local, or non-U.S. income, gross receipts, license, payroll, employment, excise, severance, stamp, occupation, premium, windfall profits, environmental, customs duties, capital stock, franchise, profits, withholding, social security (or similar), unemployment, disability, real property, personal property, sales, use, transfer, registration, value-added, alternative or add-on minimum, estimated, or other tax of any kind whatsoever, including any interest, penalty, or addition thereto, whether disputed or not, and any obligations under any agreements or arrangements with any other Person with respect to such amounts and any liability for such amounts as a result of being a member of an affiliated, consolidated, combined, or unitary group for any period.

\"**Tax Return**\" means any return, declaration, report, claim for refund, information return or statement, or other document relating to Taxes, including any schedule or attachment thereto, and including any amendment thereof.

\"**Transaction Documents**\" means this Agreement, the Escrow Agreement, and each other agreement, instrument, certificate, or document executed or delivered in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement.

\"**Transaction Expenses**\" means all fees, costs, expenses, and other amounts incurred by or on behalf of Seller or the Company (whether or not paid) in connection with the negotiation, preparation, execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement and the Transaction Documents and the consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby and thereby, including (a) all legal, accounting, tax advisory, financial advisory, consulting, and other professional fees and expenses, (b) all fees, expenses, premiums, and other amounts payable to any broker, finder, investment banker, or similar intermediary, (c) all change-of-control, transaction, retention, stay, or similar bonuses or payments payable to any employee, officer, director, or consultant of the Company in connection with or as a result of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, and (d) the employer\'s share of any payroll, social security, unemployment, or similar Taxes attributable to any of the foregoing amounts.
**Section 1.02 Interpretation**

Unless the context of this Agreement otherwise requires: (a) words of one gender include the other genders; (b) words using the singular or plural number also include the plural or singular number, respectively; (c) the terms \"hereof,\" \"herein,\" \"hereby,\" \"hereto,\" and derivative or similar words refer to this entire Agreement; (d) the terms \"Article,\" \"Section,\" \"Schedule,\" \"Exhibit,\" and \"Recital\" refer to the specified Article, Section, Schedule, Exhibit, or Recital of or to this Agreement, unless otherwise specified; (e) the word \"including\" and words of similar import shall mean \"including, without limitation,\" unless otherwise specified; (f) the word \"or\" is not exclusive; (g) all references to \"\$\" or \"dollars\" mean the lawful currency of the United States of America; (h) the word \"extent\" in the phrase \"to the extent\" shall mean the degree to which a subject or other thing extends, and such phrase shall not mean simply \"if\"; (i) references to a statute or regulation mean such statute or regulation as amended, modified, supplemented, or replaced from time to time (and, in the case of any statute, include any rules and regulations promulgated under such statute) and references to any section of any statute or regulation include any successor to such section; (j) all references to any period of days shall mean the relevant number of calendar days unless otherwise specified; (k) if the last day for giving any notice or taking any action under this Agreement is a day that is not a Business Day, then the time for giving such notice or taking such action shall be extended to the next succeeding Business Day; (l) headings of Articles and Sections are for convenience of reference only and do not affect the interpretation of this Agreement; and (m) all Exhibits and Schedules annexed hereto or referred to herein are hereby incorporated in and made a part of this Agreement as if set forth herein in full.
**[ARTICLE II]{.underline}**
**[PURCHASE AND SALE; PURCHASE PRICE]{.underline}**
**Section 2.01 Purchase and Sale of Shares**

Upon the terms and subject to the conditions of this Agreement, at the Closing, Seller shall sell, assign, transfer, convey, and deliver to Buyer, and Buyer shall purchase, acquire, and accept from Seller, all of the Shares, constituting 1,000,000 shares of common stock, par value \$0.01 per share, of the Company, which represent all of the issued and outstanding shares of capital stock of the Company, free and clear of all Encumbrances (other than restrictions arising under applicable securities Laws), for the Purchase Price, payable as provided in Sections 2.02 and 2.03.
**Section 2.02 Purchase Price**

The aggregate purchase price for the Shares (the \"Purchase Price\") shall be an amount equal to (a) the Base Enterprise Value (\$215,000,000), *plus* (b) the amount, if any, by which the Estimated Closing NWC exceeds the Target NWC, *minus* (c) the amount, if any, by which the Target NWC exceeds the Estimated Closing NWC, *minus* (d) the Estimated Closing Indebtedness, *minus* (e) the Estimated Transaction Expenses. For illustrative purposes only, based on preliminary estimates, the Purchase Price would be calculated as follows: \$215,000,000 + \$18,200,000 (Estimated Closing NWC at Target) -- \$42,300,000 (Estimated Closing Indebtedness) -- \$3,900,000 (Estimated Transaction Expenses) = \$187,000,000. The Purchase Price shall be subject to adjustment as provided in Sections 2.03 and 2.04. The Purchase Price does not include any Earnout Payment that may become payable pursuant to Section 2.05, which shall be in addition to the Purchase Price.
**Section 2.03 Closing Payment and Estimates**

**(a)** *Pre-Closing Estimate.* Not later than three (3) Business Days prior to the Closing Date, Seller shall prepare and deliver to Buyer a written statement (the \"Estimated Closing Statement\") setting forth Seller\'s good-faith estimates of: (i) the Closing NWC (the \"Estimated Closing NWC\"), (ii) the Closing Indebtedness (the \"Estimated Closing Indebtedness\"), and (iii) the Transaction Expenses (the \"Estimated Transaction Expenses\"), together with reasonable supporting documentation, schedules, and work papers used in the preparation thereof. The Estimated Closing Statement shall be prepared in accordance with the Accounting Principles and shall include a calculation of the estimated Purchase Price based on such estimates. Seller shall provide Buyer with reasonable access to the books and records of the Company and the work papers of the Company\'s accountants as Buyer may reasonably request to verify the Estimated Closing Statement. If Buyer delivers written notice of any objections to the Estimated Closing Statement within two (2) Business Days after receipt thereof, the Parties shall negotiate in good faith to resolve such objections prior to the Closing Date; *provided* that the failure of the Parties to resolve any such objections shall not delay the Closing, and the Estimated Closing Statement, as adjusted by mutual agreement of the Parties (or, absent such agreement, as originally delivered by Seller), shall be used for purposes of calculating the Closing Payment, subject to the post-Closing adjustment procedures set forth in Section 2.04.

**(b)** *Closing Payment.* At the Closing, Buyer shall pay to Seller an aggregate amount in cash (the \"Closing Payment\") equal to (i) the Purchase Price (calculated using the estimates set forth in the Estimated Closing Statement), *minus* (ii) the Escrow Amount (\$16,125,000). The Closing Payment shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds to one or more bank accounts designated in writing by Seller to Buyer no later than two (2) Business Days prior to the Closing Date.

**(c)** *Escrow Deposit.* At the Closing, Buyer shall deposit the Escrow Amount, in cash, by wire transfer of immediately available funds, with the Escrow Agent in accordance with the terms of the Escrow Agreement. The Escrow Fund shall be held, invested, and disbursed by the Escrow Agent in accordance with the terms of the Escrow Agreement. The Escrow Fund shall serve as security for Seller\'s indemnification obligations under Article IX and the post-Closing adjustment obligations under Section 2.04, as and to the extent provided herein and in the Escrow Agreement.

**(d)** *Repayment of Closing Indebtedness.* At or promptly following the Closing, Buyer shall cause the Company to repay, discharge, and satisfy in full all Closing Indebtedness. Seller shall use commercially reasonable efforts to cooperate with Buyer in connection with the repayment of such Closing Indebtedness.
**Section 2.04 Post-Closing NWC Adjustment**

**(a)** *Closing Statement.* Within ninety (90) days following the Closing Date, Buyer shall prepare and deliver to Seller a written statement (the \"Closing Statement\") setting forth Buyer\'s good-faith calculation of the actual (i) Closing NWC, (ii) Closing Indebtedness, and (iii) Transaction Expenses, together with reasonable supporting documentation, schedules, and work papers. The Closing Statement shall be prepared in accordance with the Accounting Principles and in a manner consistent with the preparation of the Estimated Closing Statement. Buyer shall provide Seller and its Representatives with reasonable access, during normal business hours and upon reasonable prior notice, to the books and records of the Company and the work papers used in the preparation of the Closing Statement.

**(b)** *Review and Objection.* Seller shall have thirty (30) days following receipt of the Closing Statement (the \"Review Period\") to review the Closing Statement. During the Review Period, Buyer shall provide Seller and its Representatives with reasonable access to the books and records of the Company, the work papers of the Company\'s accountants, and the personnel of the Company, in each case to the extent reasonably necessary for Seller\'s review of the Closing Statement. If Seller does not deliver a written notice of objection (an \"Objection Notice\") to Buyer within the Review Period, the Closing Statement as delivered by Buyer shall be deemed final and binding on the Parties. If Seller delivers an Objection Notice within the Review Period, such Objection Notice shall specify in reasonable detail each item in dispute (each, a \"Disputed Item\"), the basis for such dispute, and the amount Seller believes to be the correct amount. Any item or amount not specifically identified as a Disputed Item in the Objection Notice shall be deemed accepted by Seller and shall be final and binding on the Parties.

**(c)** *Resolution of Disputes.* If Seller delivers a timely Objection Notice, the Parties shall negotiate in good faith for a period of twenty (20) Business Days following delivery of the Objection Notice (the \"Resolution Period\") to resolve all Disputed Items. If the Parties are unable to resolve all Disputed Items within the Resolution Period, any remaining Disputed Items shall be submitted for final resolution to an independent, nationally recognized accounting firm mutually agreed upon by Buyer and Seller (the \"Independent Accountant\"); *provided* that such firm shall not be Winslow & Tate CPA Group, the auditors of the Company, or any accounting firm that has provided services to Buyer or Seller during the twenty-four (24) month period prior to such engagement. The Independent Accountant shall be engaged to resolve only the remaining Disputed Items and shall determine the correct amount of each such Disputed Item in accordance with the Accounting Principles, and such determination shall be final and binding on the Parties, absent manifest error. The Independent Accountant shall not assign a value to any Disputed Item that is greater than the highest value or less than the lowest value claimed by either Party. The Independent Accountant shall render its written determination within thirty (30) days after such engagement and shall set forth in such determination a reasoned basis for its resolution of each Disputed Item. The fees and expenses of the Independent Accountant shall be allocated between the Parties based on the relative amounts of the aggregate Disputed Items resolved in favor of each Party (as determined by the Independent Accountant), such that the Party whose positions are furthest from the Independent Accountant\'s determinations bears a proportionally greater share of such fees and expenses.
**(d)** *Adjustment Payment.* Within five (5) Business Days after the final determination of the Closing Statement (as determined pursuant to this Section 2.04):

> \(i\) If the Purchase Price as finally determined (using the actual Closing NWC, Closing Indebtedness, and Transaction Expenses as finally determined) exceeds the Purchase Price as calculated using the Estimated Closing Statement, Buyer shall pay such excess amount to Seller by wire transfer of immediately available funds.

> \(ii\) If the Purchase Price as calculated using the Estimated Closing Statement exceeds the Purchase Price as finally determined, Seller shall pay such excess amount to Buyer (first, by instructing the Escrow Agent to release such amount from the Escrow Fund, and, to the extent the Escrow Fund is insufficient, by wire transfer of immediately available funds from Seller directly to Buyer).

All adjustments pursuant to this Section 2.04 shall be made on a dollar-for-dollar basis from the first dollar of any difference, without any collar, threshold, or de minimis amount. Any adjustment amounts payable under this Section 2.04 shall bear interest from the Closing Date through the date of payment at the prime rate as published in *The Wall Street Journal* on the Closing Date (or, if the Closing Date is not a Business Day, on the immediately preceding Business Day), calculated on the basis of a 365-day year and the actual number of days elapsed.
**Section 2.05 Earnout**

**(a)** *Maximum Earnout Payment.* If the Company\'s Adjusted EBITDA for the Earnout Period (the twelve (12) month period ending December 31, 2026) equals or exceeds Thirty-Eight Million Dollars (\$38,000,000), Buyer shall pay to Seller an amount equal to Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000) (the \"Maximum Earnout Payment\").

**(b)** *Pro-Rata Earnout.* If the Company\'s Adjusted EBITDA for the Earnout Period is at least Thirty-Two Million Dollars (\$32,000,000) but less than Thirty-Eight Million Dollars (\$38,000,000), Buyer shall pay to Seller an amount (the \"Earnout Payment\") equal to: (\$25,000,000 ÷ (\$38,000,000 -- \$32,000,000)) × (Actual Adjusted EBITDA -- \$32,000,000). For the avoidance of doubt, this formula results in a linear interpolation, such that the Earnout Payment increases by approximately Four Million One Hundred Sixty-Six Thousand Six Hundred Sixty-Seven Dollars (\$4,166,667) for each One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000) of Adjusted EBITDA in excess of \$32,000,000. If the Company\'s Adjusted EBITDA for the Earnout Period is less than \$32,000,000, no Earnout Payment shall be due or payable.

**(c)** *Earnout Calculation and Dispute Resolution.* Within sixty (60) days after the end of the Earnout Period, Buyer shall prepare and deliver to Seller a written statement (the \"Earnout Statement\") setting forth Buyer\'s good-faith calculation of Adjusted EBITDA for the Earnout Period, together with reasonable supporting documentation. Seller shall have thirty (30) days to review the Earnout Statement and deliver any objections thereto. The dispute resolution procedures set forth in Section 2.04(b) and Section 2.04(c) shall apply *mutatis mutandis* to any dispute with respect to the Earnout Statement.

**(d)** *Operation of the Business During the Earnout Period.* From and after the Closing Date through the end of the Earnout Period, Buyer shall, and shall cause the Company to, operate the business of the Company in a manner consistent with past practice and in good faith to maximize the Earnout Payment. Without limiting the foregoing, Buyer shall not, and shall cause the Company not to, take any action that would reasonably be expected to reduce the Adjusted EBITDA of the Company below the levels that would otherwise have been achieved. In furtherance of the foregoing, during the Earnout Period, Buyer shall cause the Company to maintain substantially the same level of personnel, equipment, and other resources as in effect immediately prior to the Closing Date and shall not divert or redirect any contracts, customers, revenues, or business opportunities of the Company to Buyer or any of its Affiliates. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Buyer acknowledges and agrees that Seller shall have no obligation to contribute resources, personnel, or funds to the Company during the Earnout Period, and the obligations set forth in this Section 2.05(d) are solely obligations of Buyer.

**(e)** *Payment of Earnout.* Any Earnout Payment determined to be payable pursuant to this Section 2.05 shall be paid by Buyer to Seller within ten (10) Business Days after the final determination of Adjusted EBITDA for the Earnout Period (whether by agreement of the Parties, expiration of the review period without objection, or determination of the Independent Accountant), by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account designated by Seller. For U.S. federal income tax purposes, the Parties agree to treat any Earnout Payment as an adjustment to the Purchase Price.
**Section 2.06 Withholding**

Buyer and the Company shall be entitled to deduct and withhold from any amounts payable pursuant to this Agreement such amounts as Buyer, the Company, or the Escrow Agent may be required to deduct and withhold under the Code, or any applicable provision of state, local, or non-U.S. Tax Law, with respect to the making of any such payment. To the extent that amounts are so withheld and remitted to the applicable Governmental Authority, such withheld amounts shall be treated for all purposes of this Agreement as having been paid to the Person in respect of which such deduction and withholding was made.
**Section 2.07 Closing**

The closing of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement (the \"Closing\") shall take place remotely via the electronic exchange of documents and signatures on the date that is three (3) Business Days after the date on which all of the conditions set forth in Article VII have been satisfied or waived (other than those conditions that by their nature are to be satisfied at the Closing, but subject to the satisfaction or waiver of such conditions at the Closing), or at such other time, date, and place as the Parties may mutually agree in writing (the \"Closing Date\"). The Parties anticipate that the Closing will occur in mid-January 2026. The Closing shall be deemed to be effective as of 12:01 a.m. Eastern Time on the Closing Date.
**Section 2.08 Closing Deliverables**
**(a)** *Seller Deliverables.* At the Closing, Seller shall deliver, or cause to be delivered, to Buyer the following:

> \(i\) stock certificates representing all of the Shares, duly endorsed in blank or accompanied by duly executed stock powers, with all required transfer stamps affixed, sufficient to transfer to Buyer good and valid title to all of the Shares, free and clear of all Encumbrances;

> \(ii\) a certificate of good standing (or equivalent certificate) for the Company issued by the Secretary of State of the State of Oregon, and certificates of good standing (or equivalent certificates) for the Company issued by the Secretaries of State of each of the States of Washington, California, and Nevada, in each case dated not more than ten (10) days prior to the Closing Date;

> \(iii\) certified copies of the resolutions duly adopted by the board of directors of Seller authorizing the execution, delivery, and performance by Seller of this Agreement and the Transaction Documents and the consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby and thereby;

> \(iv\) a certificate of non-foreign status of Seller, executed pursuant to Treasury Regulation Section 1.1445-2(b)(2), in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to Buyer (the \"FIRPTA Certificate\");

lines.text: **Section 2.07 Closing**

The closing of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement (the \"Closing\") shall take place remotely via the electronic exchange of documents and signatures on the date that is three (3) Business Days after the date on which all of the conditions set forth in Article VII have been satisfied or waived (other than those conditions that by their nature are to be satisfied at the Closing, but subject to the satisfaction or waiver of such conditions at the Closing), or at such other time, date, and place as the Parties may mutually agree in writing (the \"Closing Date\"). The Parties anticipate that the Closing will occur in mid-January 2026. The Closing shall be deemed to be effective as of 12:01 a.m. Eastern Time on the Closing Date.
**Section 2.08 Closing Deliverables**
**(a)** *Seller Deliverables.* At the Closing, Seller shall deliver, or cause to be delivered, to Buyer the following:

> \(i\) stock certificates representing all of the Shares, duly endorsed in blank or accompanied by duly executed stock powers, with all required transfer stamps affixed, sufficient to transfer to Buyer good and valid title to all of the Shares, free and clear of all Encumbrances;

> \(ii\) a certificate of good standing (or equivalent certificate) for the Company issued by the Secretary of State of the State of Oregon, and certificates of good standing (or equivalent certificates) for the Company issued by the Secretaries of State of each of the States of Washington, California, and Nevada, in each case dated not more than ten (10) days prior to the Closing Date;

> \(iii\) certified copies of the resolutions duly adopted by the board of directors of Seller authorizing the execution, delivery, and performance by Seller of this Agreement and the Transaction Documents and the consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby and thereby;

> \(iv\) a certificate of non-foreign status of Seller, executed pursuant to Treasury Regulation Section 1.1445-2(b)(2), in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to Buyer (the \"FIRPTA Certificate\");
> \(v\) the Escrow Agreement, duly executed by Seller;
> \(vi\) written resignations, effective as of the Closing, of each director and officer of the Company designated by Buyer in writing at least five (5) Business Days prior to the Closing Date;

> \(vii\) evidence reasonably satisfactory to Buyer that all contracts, agreements, and arrangements between the Company and Seller or any Affiliate of Seller (other than the affiliate lease described on Schedule 4.09, which shall be addressed separately by the Parties) have been terminated effective as of or prior to the Closing without any remaining liability of the Company;

> \(viii\) a certificate of an authorized officer of Seller, dated as of the Closing Date, certifying that the conditions set forth in Section 7.02(a), Section 7.02(b), and Section 7.02(c) have been satisfied; and

> \(ix\) a certificate of the secretary or an assistant secretary of Seller, dated as of the Closing Date, certifying as to (A) the certificate of incorporation and bylaws of Seller, (B) the articles of incorporation and bylaws of the Company, and (C) the incumbency and specimen signatures of the officers of Seller executing this Agreement and the Transaction Documents.
**(b)** *Buyer Deliverables.* At the Closing, Buyer shall deliver, or cause to be delivered, to Seller the following:
> \(i\) the Closing Payment, by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account or accounts designated in writing by Seller in accordance with Section 2.03(b);
> \(ii\) the Escrow Amount, by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the Escrow Agent in accordance with Section 2.03(c) and the Escrow Agreement;

> \(iii\) certified copies of the resolutions duly adopted by the members or managers of Buyer (as applicable) authorizing the execution, delivery, and performance by Buyer of this Agreement and the Transaction Documents and the consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby and thereby;
> \(iv\) the Escrow Agreement, duly executed by Buyer;

> \(v\) a certificate of an authorized officer or manager of Buyer, dated as of the Closing Date, certifying that the conditions set forth in Section 7.03(a) and Section 7.03(b) have been satisfied; and
> \(vi\) evidence of Buyer\'s organizational good standing issued by the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware, dated not more than ten (10) days prior to the Closing Date.

**[REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES OF SELLER]{.underline}**

Seller is a corporation duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the State of Delaware. 189: **[3.3 Environmental-Sector-Specific Covenants]{.underline}**
190: 
191: In addition to the general interim operating covenants set forth in Section 3.1 and the affiliate transaction restrictions set forth in Section 3.2, the SPA for an environmental services acquisition must include the following sector-specific interim covenants:
192: 
193: > \(a\) **Environmental Permits.** Maintain all Environmental Permits in full force and effect; do not take any action, or fail to take any action, that could reasonably be expected to result in the revocation, suspension, modification, non-renewal, or material limitation of any Environmental Permit held by the Company.
194: >
195: > \(b\) **Active Remediation Projects.** Continue all active remediation and environmental response projects in the ordinary course of business and in compliance with all applicable orders, consent decrees, administrative agreements, remediation action plans, and other governmental requirements. Do not voluntarily suspend, terminate, or materially alter the scope of any active remediation project without the buyer\'s prior written consent.
196: >
197: > \(c\) **New Environmental Remediation Contracts.** Do not enter into any new environmental remediation or response contract or agreement with a contract value exceeding \$500,000 (or such other threshold as may be agreed) without the buyer\'s prior written consent.
198: >
199: > \(d\) **Environmental Insurance.** Maintain all environmental impairment liability insurance policies, pollution legal liability insurance policies, and contractor\'s pollution liability insurance policies in full force and effect, with coverage levels no less than those in effect as of the date of the agreement.
200: >
201: > \(e\) **Notice of Environmental Claims.** Provide prompt written notice to the buyer (and in no event later than five (5) business days after the Company\'s receipt thereof) of any new environmental claim, notice of violation, information request under CERCLA Section 104(e), RCRA Section 3007, or any analogous state law provision, consent order, administrative complaint, or other regulatory action received by the Company during the Interim Period.
202: >
203: > \(f\) **Settlement of Environmental Claims.** Do not settle, compromise, or consent to the entry of any judgment with respect to any environmental claim, proceeding, or regulatory action involving potential liability in excess of \$250,000 (or such other threshold as may be agreed) without the buyer\'s prior written consent.
204:
