# Article I
add_text(doc,'Article I — Definitions','Heading 1')
add_issue(doc,1,'Section 1.01','Material Adverse Effect — disproportionate-impact exceptions','Critical',
'''"Material Adverse Effect" means any event, change, effect, development, state of facts, condition, circumstance, or occurrence that, individually or in the aggregate, has had or would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on (a) the business, assets, liabilities, financial condition, or results of operations of the Company, or (b) the ability of Seller to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement; provided, however, that none of the following, individually or in the aggregate, shall be deemed to constitute, or shall be taken into account in determining whether there has been or would reasonably be expected to be, a Material Adverse Effect: (i) changes in general economic, financial, credit, securities market, or political conditions in the United States or globally; (ii) changes in conditions generally affecting the environmental services industry; (iii) changes in Environmental Laws or regulations; (iv) changes in GAAP or applicable Law (other than Environmental Laws, which are addressed in clause (iii) above); ...''',
'''"Material Adverse Effect" means any event, change, effect, development, state of facts, condition, circumstance, or occurrence that, individually or in the aggregate, has had or would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on (a) the business, assets, liabilities, financial condition, or results of operations of the Company, or (b) the ability of Seller to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement; provided, however, that none of the following, individually or in the aggregate, shall be deemed to constitute, or shall be taken into account in determining whether there has been or would reasonably be expected to be, a Material Adverse Effect: (i) changes in general economic, financial, credit, securities market, or political conditions in the United States or globally; (ii) changes in conditions generally affecting the environmental services industry; (iii) changes in Environmental Laws or regulations; (iv) changes in GAAP or applicable Law (other than Environmental Laws, which are addressed in clause (iii) above); (v) acts of war (whether or not declared), armed hostilities, sabotage, terrorism, military actions, or any escalation or worsening thereof, epidemics, pandemics, earthquakes, hurricanes, tornados, floods, or other natural disasters or acts of God; (vi) the announcement or pendency of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, including any impact on relationships with customers, suppliers, employees, or Governmental Authorities; (vii) any action taken by the Company at the express written request or with the express written consent of Buyer; and (viii) any failure by the Company to meet any internal or external projections, forecasts, or estimates of revenue, earnings, or other financial performance metrics for any period (provided that the underlying facts, circumstances, and causes of any such failure may be considered in determining whether a Material Adverse Effect has occurred); provided, further, that changes, effects, events, or developments described in clauses (i) through (v) shall be taken into account in determining whether a Material Adverse Effect has occurred or would reasonably be expected to occur to the extent such changes, effects, events, or developments disproportionately affect the Company and its Subsidiaries, taken as a whole, relative to other participants in the industries in which the Company and its Subsidiaries operate.''',
'''The industry and regulatory carve-outs are unacceptable without a disproportionate-impact exception. Cascadia is itself an environmental-services business; an industry downturn or regulatory change that affects Cascadia materially more than peers must remain available for the MAE analysis. The proposed language also preserves the existing general carve-outs while preventing them from excluding target-specific CERCLA, RCRA, permitting, or regulatory harm.''',
'''Term Sheet §§7 and 12 (MAE representation and closing condition); Playbook §§2.1–2.2 (mandatory disproportionate-impact qualifier and environmental regulatory exposure); DD Memo §§III, V, and VI (Dalton Creek, permit, and government-contract risks).''')
add_issue(doc,2,'Section 1.01','Indemnification Cap — conform to the term sheet','High',
'''"Indemnification Cap" means Forty-Three Million Dollars ($43,000,000), which is equal to twenty percent (20%) of the Base Enterprise Value.''',
'''"Indemnification Cap" means Twenty-Six Million Eight Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand Dollars ($26,875,000), which is equal to twelve and one-half percent (12.5%) of the Base Enterprise Value.''',
'''The seller draft increases the general cap from the agreed 12.5% to 20% of enterprise value. This is a direct economic deviation, not a drafting judgment. The definition must be corrected and the operative cap in Section 9.04(b) must be conformed.''',
'''Term Sheet §8 (General Indemnification Cap); Playbook §5.1 (cap must match executed term sheet; 12.5% firm target); DD Memo §III (known environmental exposure supports preserving the negotiated cap structure).''')

# Article II
add_text(doc,'Article II — Purchase and Sale; Purchase Price','Heading 1')
add_issue(doc,3,'Section 2.05(d)','Earnout operational covenant — remove affirmative obligations','Critical',
'''From and after the Closing Date through the end of the Earnout Period, Buyer shall, and shall cause the Company to, operate the business of the Company in a manner consistent with past practice and in good faith to maximize the Earnout Payment. Without limiting the foregoing, Buyer shall not, and shall cause the Company not to, take any action that would reasonably be expected to reduce the Adjusted EBITDA of the Company below the levels that would otherwise have been achieved. In furtherance of the foregoing, during the Earnout Period, Buyer shall cause the Company to maintain substantially the same level of personnel, equipment, and other resources as in effect immediately prior to the Closing Date and shall not divert or redirect any contracts, customers, revenues, or business opportunities of the Company to Buyer or any of its Affiliates.''',
'''Following the Closing, Buyer shall not, and shall cause the Company not to, take any action with the primary purpose of reducing or avoiding the Earnout Payment. For the avoidance of doubt, nothing in this Section 2.05(d) shall restrict Buyer\'s right to operate, integrate, restructure, or otherwise manage the Company and its business in Buyer\'s sole discretion, including the right to make capital expenditure decisions, change pricing, make personnel decisions, make strategic investments, acquire or dispose of businesses or assets, allocate corporate resources, restructure the Company or its business, and modify operations, and no such action shall constitute a breach of this Section 2.05(d) unless taken with the primary purpose of reducing or avoiding the Earnout Payment. Buyer shall have no obligation to maintain the Company as a separate entity, maintain any particular level of capital expenditures, retain any particular employees, or refrain from any operational decision, so long as Buyer does not take such action with the primary purpose of reducing or avoiding the Earnout Payment.''',
'''The seller\'s language would constrain integration, restructuring, bolt-on acquisitions, personnel decisions, and resource allocation for the entire earnout period and creates litigation risk over ordinary business judgment. The only acceptable buyer covenant is the narrow primary-purpose negative covenant. Sections 2.05(a)–(c) correctly reflect the $25 million maximum, $38 million full-payment threshold, $32 million floor, linear interpolation, and December 31, 2026 measurement period; no change is needed to those mechanics except to ensure Exhibit D is consistent.''',
'''Term Sheet §5 (earnout economics and negative covenant); Playbook §7.1–7.2 (no affirmative operational obligations; primary-purpose standard); DD Memo §§III–VI (buyer must retain flexibility to manage a platform with environmental projects and government contracts).''')
add_issue(doc,4,'Sections 2.03(d), 2.08(a), and 7.02','Closing debt payoff — payoff letters, funds flow, and closing condition','High',
'''At or promptly following the Closing, Buyer shall cause the Company to repay, discharge, and satisfy in full all Closing Indebtedness. Seller shall use commercially reasonable efforts to cooperate with Buyer in connection with the repayment of such Closing Indebtedness.''',
'''(d) Closing Indebtedness shall be repaid, discharged, and satisfied in full simultaneously with the Closing through the closing funds flow. Seller shall deliver, or cause to be delivered, to Buyer executed payoff letters from each holder of Target Indebtedness no later than three (3) Business Days prior to the Closing Date, including Cascade Mutual Bank with respect to the $28,000,000 senior term loan, Pacific Lease Corp. with respect to the $9,800,000 equipment financing facility, and Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc. with respect to the $4,500,000 subordinated seller note. Each payoff letter shall state the total amount required to repay the applicable obligation in full as of the Closing Date, including principal, accrued and unpaid interest, prepayment premiums, breakage costs, fees, and other amounts required to discharge the obligation; provide wire transfer instructions; and provide for the release of all liens and other security interests upon receipt of the payoff amount, including delivery of applicable UCC termination statements and other lien-release documents. Buyer shall cause the applicable payoff amounts to be paid directly to the applicable holders at the Closing in accordance with the payoff letters and the Funds Flow Agreement. No Target Indebtedness shall remain outstanding after the Closing.''',
'''The seller draft permits repayment after closing and contains no payoff-letter timing, content, or funding mechanics. This is inconsistent with the executed term sheet and the requirements of Clearwater Environmental Lending Corp. Add the above as a pre-closing deliverable and add the following condition to Section 7.02: “Payoff Letters. Seller shall have delivered the payoff letters required by Section 2.03(d) no later than three (3) Business Days prior to the Closing Date, and such payoff letters shall remain in full force and effect as of the Closing.” Add a corresponding seller deliverable in Section 2.08(a) and require the Funds Flow Agreement to include all debt payoffs.''',
'''Term Sheet §6 (three-business-day payoff letters, simultaneous payoff, funds flow, and condition); Playbook §§9.2 and 13.1(f); DD Memo §VI (government contracts and material operating continuity; debt payoff is also required by the buyer lender).''')

# Article IV
add_text(doc,'Article IV — Representations and Warranties Regarding the Company','Heading 1')
add_issue(doc,5,'Section 4.16','Government contracts — change-of-control and novation representations','Critical',
'''(a) The Company is a party to four (4) active government contracts ... with the Oregon Department of Environmental Quality, the Washington Department of Ecology, the United States Army Corps of Engineers, and the Bureau of Land Management (collectively, the “Government Contracts”). (b) Each Government Contract is in full force and effect ... (c) Neither the Company nor any of its directors, officers, or employees is subject to debarment ... (d) The Company has complied in all material respects with all applicable procurement Laws, regulations, and requirements in connection with the Government Contracts.''',
'''Section 4.16 Government Contracts. (a) The Company is a party to the four (4) active Government Contracts listed on Schedule 4.16: the Oregon Department of Environmental Quality contract, the Washington Department of Ecology contract, the United States Army Corps of Engineers contract, and the Bureau of Land Management contract. Seller has delivered to Buyer true, correct, and complete copies of each Government Contract, including all amendments, modifications, task orders, solicitations, and related correspondence. (b) Each Government Contract is in full force and effect and is a legal, valid, and binding obligation of the Company and, to the Knowledge of the Company, the applicable Governmental Authority. Neither the Company nor, to the Knowledge of the Company, any other party is in material breach or default, and no event has occurred that, with notice or lapse of time, would constitute a material breach or default. (c) No Government Contract is subject to a pending or, to the Knowledge of the Company, threatened termination for default or convenience, suspension, non-renewal, material modification, or loss of funding. (d) Neither the Company nor any director, officer, employee, or subcontractor of the Company is subject to debarment, suspension, proposed debarment, proposed suspension, or any exclusion from contracting with any Governmental Authority. (e) The Company has complied in all material respects with all applicable procurement Laws, regulations, and requirements, including the Anti-Assignment Act, 41 U.S.C. § 6305, and applicable FAR Part 42 requirements, and has made all required disclosures and submissions. (f) Except as set forth on Schedule 4.16, no consent, approval, novation agreement, recognition agreement, change-of-name agreement, or other notice is required from any contracting officer or other Governmental Authority as a result of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement; and, to the Knowledge of the Company, no contracting officer has indicated an intent to terminate, suspend, materially modify, or refuse to recognize any Government Contract as a result of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement. (g) Schedule 4.16 identifies, for each Government Contract, any required change-of-control notice, consent, novation agreement, recognition agreement, or other approval and the status of each required submission.''',
'''The existing reps identify the four contracts but do not allocate the specific change-of-control/novation risk. The federal contracts are subject to the Anti-Assignment Act and FAR 42.12; the state contracts require separate review. The revised language requires complete contract copies, status and termination representations, and a schedule of required notices/approvals so that Buyer can measure the risk and enforce the pre- and post-closing covenants.''',
'''Term Sheet §7 (government-contract representations); Playbook §12.2 (government-contract representation, novation covenant, and closing-condition analysis); DD Memo §VI (four active contracts, federal FAR 42.1204 risk, and material revenue/backlog exposure).''')
add_issue(doc,6,'Sections 4.15, 4.16, and 4.17','Environmental sector representations — permit, remediation, and insurance status','High',
'''The Company holds all Environmental Permits necessary for the conduct of its business as currently conducted, and all such Environmental Permits are in full force and effect. ... No Action is pending or, to the Knowledge of the Company, threatened to revoke, suspend, cancel, terminate, modify, or not renew any Environmental Permit. ... The Company maintains environmental impairment liability insurance ... and project-specific environmental liability insurance relating to the Hargrove Industrial Site.''',
'''Add the following sentence at the end of Section 4.15(b): “No Environmental Permit is subject to any pending or, to the Knowledge of the Company, threatened change-of-control notice, approval, transfer, re-issuance, or other regulatory process, except as set forth on Schedule 4.15(b), and Schedule 4.15(b) identifies each such requirement and its status.” Add the following to Section 4.15(f): “All premiums due under each environmental insurance policy have been paid, each such policy is in full force and effect, and no notice of cancellation, non-renewal, rescission, reservation of rights, or material modification has been received.” Add the following sentence at the end of Section 4.16: “The Government Contracts and all related novation, recognition, and change-of-control requirements are accurately described on Schedule 4.16.”''',
'''The draft lists 23 permits and the environmental policies but does not state whether change-of-control notifications/approvals are required or identify their status. The revised language converts the diligence findings into schedule-level representations. Hargrove has approximately $4.2 million of remaining cost and relies on a $10 million site-specific policy; the insurance representation should therefore cover payment status and adverse notices.''',
'''Term Sheet §7 (environmental matters, government contracts, and insurance); Playbook §§3.3, 12.1, and 13.2; DD Memo §§IV, V, VI, and VII (Hargrove, 23 permits, government contracts, and insurance program).''')

# Article VI
add_text(doc,'Article VI — Covenants','Heading 1')
add_issue(doc,7,'Section 6.01(b)','Affiliate transaction restriction during the interim period','High',
'''Without limiting the generality of Section 6.01(a), ... Seller shall not permit the Company to: (i) amend, modify, or restate the articles of incorporation ... (xiii) enter into any non-competition, non-solicitation, exclusive dealing, or similar restrictive covenant agreement.''',
'''Add the following as new Section 6.01(b)(xiv): “enter into any Contract, transaction, or arrangement with, amend, modify, extend, renew, supplement, or terminate any existing Contract, transaction, or arrangement with, or make any payment or transfer any asset to, in each case directly or indirectly, Seller, any Affiliate of Seller, or any officer, director, manager, shareholder, member, partner, or family member of Seller or any Affiliate of Seller, other than compensation payments to employees in the ordinary course of business consistent with past practice, without the prior written consent of Buyer, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed.”''',
'''The draft discloses the $1.6 million annual above-market Affiliate Lease but does not stop Seller from expanding, amending, extending, renewing, prepaying, or adding affiliate arrangements before closing. The covenant should cover both new and existing arrangements and should preserve Buyer consent over value leakage.''',
'''Term Sheet §7 (affiliate arrangements reflected in valuation); Playbook §§3.2 and 3.2 sample covenant; DD Memo §II (above-market affiliate rent adjustment) and §V (permit-dependent operating facilities).''')
add_issue(doc,8,'New Section 6.06','Government-contract novation/recognition and post-closing cooperation covenant','Critical',
'''Section 6.05 Third-Party Consents. Seller shall, and shall cause the Company to, use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain ... all consents, waivers, approvals, authorizations, and notices required ... including those set forth on Schedule 4.05.''',
'''Insert the following as new Section 6.06 and renumber the current Sections 6.06 through 6.11 accordingly: “Government Contracts; Novation and Recognition. (a) From the date of this Agreement until the Closing Date, Seller shall cause the Company to promptly notify each applicable federal and state contracting officer of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement and to prepare and submit all requests, notices, and supporting materials required to obtain any novation agreement, recognition agreement, change-of-name agreement, consent, approval, or other acknowledgement required under the Anti-Assignment Act, 41 U.S.C. § 6305, FAR Part 42, Subpart 42.12, or applicable state procurement Law. (b) Seller and the Company shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain each required novation agreement, recognition agreement, consent, approval, or written confirmation that the applicable process is underway and that the Company may continue interim performance pending completion. Seller shall provide Buyer copies of all submissions and material communications within two (2) Business Days after delivery or receipt and shall not make any material submission or agree to any material modification of a Government Contract without Buyer\'s prior written consent. (c) Seller shall cause the Company to continue performing each Government Contract in compliance with its terms pending completion of the applicable process. (d) Following the Closing, Seller shall reasonably cooperate, at no material cost to Seller, with Buyer and the Company for twelve (12) months, or longer if reasonably necessary to complete a pending process, including by executing documents, providing historical information, and participating in meetings with contracting officers. Seller shall cause its Affiliates to provide the same cooperation.”''',
'''A generic third-party-consent clause is not enough for four material government contracts. The two federal contracts may require novation under FAR 42.1204, and loss of a contract could terminate a material revenue stream. Because agency timing may exceed the Outside Date, the recommended position is mandatory submission, reasonable-best-efforts cooperation, no adverse government signal, and a post-closing tail rather than an absolute requirement that every novation be completed before closing. Discuss with Marcus whether to make receipt of novation/recognition a hard condition for the federal contracts.''',
'''Term Sheet §7 and §12 (government-contract representations and closing conditions); Playbook §12.2 and §13.2(a); DD Memo §VI.C (submit before closing, no denial/termination signal, and post-closing cooperation).''')
add_issue(doc,9,'New Section 6.07','Environmental permits, remediation projects, insurance, and notice covenant','Medium',
'''Section 6.01(a)(iii) requires the Company to maintain “all insurance policies of the Company or replacement policies with comparable coverage on terms no less favorable in the aggregate.” There is no covenant addressing permit-change notifications, post-closing permit cooperation, active remediation, or environmental notices.''',
'''Insert the following as new Section 6.07 and renumber the current Sections 6.06 through 6.11 accordingly: “Environmental Permits and Projects. (a) Prior to the Closing, Seller shall cause the Company to identify each Environmental Permit requiring notification to or approval from an issuing Governmental Authority as a result of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, prepare and submit all required notifications and applications, and provide Buyer copies of each submission and each material response. (b) From the date of this Agreement through the Closing, Seller shall cause the Company to maintain all Environmental Permits and all environmental impairment liability, pollution legal liability, contractor\'s pollution liability, and site-specific environmental insurance policies in full force and effect at coverage levels no less than those in effect on the date hereof; continue the Hargrove Industrial Site remediation in the ordinary course and in compliance with applicable orders, work plans, and Government Contracts; and not voluntarily suspend, terminate, or materially alter any active remediation project without Buyer\'s prior written consent. (c) Seller shall cause the Company to provide Buyer written notice within five (5) Business Days after receipt of any environmental claim, notice of violation, CERCLA § 104(e) or RCRA § 3007 information request, consent order, administrative complaint, or other material regulatory action. (d) For twelve (12) months following the Closing, or longer to the extent reasonably necessary to complete a pending process, Seller shall reasonably cooperate with Buyer and the Company in completing any permit notification, transfer, re-issuance, amendment, or approval process, including by executing documents, providing historical information, and participating in agency communications.”''',
'''The stock structure preserves the permit-holding entity but does not eliminate change-of-control notifications. The covenant addresses the 23-permit portfolio and the four-state regulatory footprint, protects the active Hargrove project and its insurance, and gives Buyer prompt visibility into new environmental claims. The post-closing tail is necessary because agency review may extend beyond closing.''',
'''Term Sheet §7 (environmental matters and insurance); Playbook §§3.3, 12.1, and 13.2(b)–(d); DD Memo §§IV, V, and VII (Hargrove, 23 permits, state notification requirements, and environmental insurance).''')
add_issue(doc,10,'Section 6.09(a) and (b)','Non-competition and non-solicitation — conform to term sheet','Medium',
'''(a) For a period of five (5) years following the Closing Date, Seller shall not ... be connected with any business anywhere in the United States. (b) For a period of three (3) years ... Seller shall not ... solicit, recruit, hire, or engage any employee ... or solicit or encourage any customer, supplier, licensee, licensor, or other business relationship ...''',
'''Replace Section 6.09(a) with: “(a) Non-Competition. For a period of three (3) years following the Closing Date, Seller shall not, and shall cause its controlled Affiliates not to, directly or indirectly, engage in, own, manage, operate, finance, control, or participate in the ownership, management, operation, or control of any business engaged in the provision of environmental remediation services or hazardous waste management services, as such services are conducted by the Company as of the Closing Date, in the States of Oregon, Washington, California, or Nevada; provided that this Section 6.09(a) shall not restrict (i) any portfolio company or operating subsidiary of Seller that is not engaged in environmental remediation or hazardous waste management as of the Closing Date, (ii) Seller\'s existing construction and timber operations, (iii) passive ownership of less than five percent (5%) of the outstanding equity securities of a publicly traded entity, or (iv) environmental-related activities incidental to and performed solely in connection with Seller\'s construction or timber operations.” Replace Section 6.09(b) with: “(b) Non-Solicitation. For a period of two (2) years following the Closing Date, Seller shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to, directly or indirectly, solicit, recruit, hire, or engage any individual who is an employee of the Company as of the Closing Date, or induce, encourage, or attempt to induce or encourage any such employee to terminate employment with the Company; provided that this Section 6.09(b) shall not restrict general solicitations not specifically directed to Company employees or the hiring of an employee who contacts Seller or its Affiliates on the employee\'s own initiative without solicitation.”''',
'''The five-year nationwide “any business” restriction would sweep in Evergreen\'s construction and timber operations and creates enforceability risk. The term sheet specifies a three-year, four-state restriction limited to environmental remediation and hazardous waste management, with express construction/timber carve-outs. The existing three-year employee/customer non-solicit also conflicts with the term sheet\'s two-year employee-only covenant.''',
'''Term Sheet §11 (duration, geography, business scope, bound parties, carve-outs, and two-year non-solicit); Playbook §10.1 (tailored scope and enforceability); DD Memo §II (Company operates in Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada; Seller has unrelated operations).''')

# Article VII
add_text(doc,'Article VII — Conditions to Closing','Heading 1')
add_issue(doc,11,'Section 7.02','Buyer closing conditions — payoff, government-contract status, permits, insurance, and R&W Insurance','Critical',
'''The obligations of Buyer ... shall be subject to ... (a) Representations and Warranties; (b) Covenants; (c) No Material Adverse Effect; (d) Officer\'s Certificate; (e) Seller Deliverables; (f) Third-Party Consents; and (g) Escrow Agreement.''',
'''Add the following new conditions to Section 7.02 and renumber the existing Section 7.02(g) as Section 7.02(k): “(g) Payoff Letters. Seller shall have delivered the payoff letters required by Section 2.03(d) no later than three (3) Business Days prior to the Closing Date, and each payoff letter shall remain effective and provide for release of the applicable liens upon payment. (h) Government Contracts. All required novation, recognition, change-of-name, consent, approval, and change-of-control submissions for the Government Contracts shall have been timely submitted; no applicable Governmental Authority shall have denied such request or notified Seller or the Company of an intent to terminate, suspend, materially modify, or refuse to recognize any Government Contract as a result of the transactions; and, for each Government Contract for which final novation or recognition has not been obtained, the applicable contracting officer shall have provided written confirmation that the process is underway and that interim performance will be permitted. (i) Environmental Permits and Insurance. All notifications required by applicable Law in connection with a change of control of the Company\'s Environmental Permits shall have been submitted, all approvals required before the Closing shall have been obtained, and the environmental insurance policies described in Section 4.15(f) shall be in full force and effect. (j) R&W Insurance. If Buyer elects to obtain a representations and warranties insurance policy, Buyer shall have received evidence reasonably satisfactory to Buyer that the policy has been bound and is in full force and effect.”''',
'''The draft has no debt payoff condition and no separate government-contract or environmental-sector condition. Because full agency novation may take 60–120 days or longer, the buyer-side compromise is to require submission, no adverse agency action, and written permission for interim performance rather than insist on completed novation as an absolute condition. Client decision is required on whether to elevate final novation/recognition to a hard condition for the two federal contracts.''',
'''Term Sheet §§6, 7, and 12 (payoff condition, government-contract conditions, and environmental/insurance representations); Playbook §§9.2, 12.2, 13.1, and 13.2; DD Memo §§V–VII.''')

# Article IX
add_text(doc,'Article IX — Indemnification','Heading 1')
add_issue(doc,12,'Section 9.01','Environmental representation survival — minimum 36 months','High',
'''(b) All representations and warranties contained in this Agreement (other than the Fundamental Representations) shall survive the Closing and continue in full force and effect for a period of twelve (12) months following the Closing Date, and shall thereupon expire and be of no further force or effect.''',
'''Replace Section 9.01 with: “(a) The Fundamental Representations shall survive the Closing and continue in full force and effect until the date that is sixty (60) days following the expiration of the applicable statute of limitations relating to the matters covered thereby, giving effect to any waiver, mitigation, or extension thereof. (b) The Tax Representations shall survive the Closing until sixty (60) days following the expiration of the applicable statute of limitations relating to the matters covered thereby, giving effect to any waiver, mitigation, or extension thereof. (c) The representations and warranties in Sections 4.15 (Environmental Matters), 4.16 (Government Contracts) to the extent relating to environmental or regulatory compliance, and 4.17 (Insurance) to the extent relating to environmental insurance (collectively, the “Environmental Representations”) shall survive the Closing for thirty-six (36) months following the Closing Date. Buyer reserves the right to seek survival of the Environmental Representations through the full applicable statute of limitations, including any period applicable to CERCLA cost-recovery or contribution claims. (d) All other representations and warranties, other than the Fundamental Representations, Tax Representations, and Environmental Representations, shall survive the Closing for eighteen (18) months following the Closing Date. (e) Covenants and agreements that by their terms are to be performed after the Closing shall survive in accordance with their terms; covenants and agreements to be performed before or at the Closing shall survive for twelve (12) months following the Closing Date. (f) No claim may be asserted after the applicable survival period; provided that a claim properly asserted in writing before expiration shall survive until finally resolved.”''',
'''A uniform 12-month survival period is inadequate for environmental liabilities that may take years to crystallize. The minimum buyer position is 36 months, with a preferred full-statute position for CERCLA-related matters. The proposed clause also corrects the draft\'s separate problem that general non-Fundamental representations receive only 12 months, versus the 18-month term-sheet period and the playbook\'s 18–24 month range.''',
'''Term Sheet §8 (18-month general and minimum 36-month environmental survival); Playbook §§4.1–4.2 (environmental minimum and full-statute preference); DD Memo §§III–V (CERCLA latency, active remediation timeline, and permit risk).''')
add_issue(doc,13,'Section 9.02 and new Section 9.09','Dalton Creek Special Indemnity — known CERCLA exposure','High',
'''Section 9.02 lists indemnification for (a) representation breaches, (b) covenant breaches, (c) unpaid Transaction Expenses, and (d) Pre-Closing Taxes. The draft contains no separate indemnity for Dalton Creek; the only reference is the disclosure of the EPA information request on Schedule 4.19.''',
'''Add the following as new Section 9.02(e): “any Losses arising out of, resulting from, or relating to the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity set forth in Section 9.09.” Insert the following as new Section 9.09: “Dalton Creek Special Indemnity. def set_cell_shading(cell, fill):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd = tcPr.find(qn('w:shd'))
    if shd is None:
        shd = OxmlElement('w:shd')
        tcPr.append(shd)
    shd.set(qn('w:fill'), fill)

def set_cell_border(cell, **kwargs):
    tc = cell._tc
    tcPr = tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    tcBorders = tcPr.first_child_found_in('w:tcBorders')
    if tcBorders is None:
        tcBorders = OxmlElement('w:tcBorders')
        tcPr.append(tcBorders)
    for edge in ('top','left','bottom','right','insideH','insideV'):
        if edge in kwargs:
            tag = 'w:{}'.format(edge)
            element = tcBorders.find(qn(tag))
            if element is None:
                element = OxmlElement(tag)
                tcBorders.append(element)
            for key, value in kwargs[edge].items():
                element.set(qn('w:{}'.format(key)), str(value))

def set_repeat_table_header(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    tblHeader = OxmlElement('w:tblHeader')
    tblHeader.set(qn('w:val'), 'true')
    trPr.append(tblHeader)

def set_cell_margins(cell, top=90, start=100, bottom=90, end=100):
    tc = cell._tc
    tcPr = tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    tcMar = tcPr.first_child_found_in('w:tcMar')
    if tcMar is None:
        tcMar = OxmlElement('w:tcMar')
        tcPr.append(tcMar)
    for m, v in [('top', top), ('start', start), ('bottom', bottom), ('end', end)]:
        node = tcMar.find(qn('w:'+m))
        if node is None:
            node = OxmlElement('w:'+m)
            tcMar.append(node)

    instrText = OxmlElement('w:instrText'); instrText.set(qn('xml:space'), 'preserve'); instrText.text = ' PAGE '
    fldChar2 = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); fldChar2.set(qn('w:fldCharType'), 'end')
    r = paragraph.add_run()._r
    r.append(fldChar1); r.append(instrText); r.append(fldChar2)

def add_text(doc, text, style=None, bold=False, italic=False, color=None, size=None, align=None, space_after=4):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style=style)
    if align is not None: p.alignment = align
    r = p.add_run(text)
    r.bold = bold; r.italic = italic
    if color: r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(*color)
    if size: r.font.size = Pt(size)
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(space_after)
    return p

def add_mixed(doc, parts, style=None, space_after=4):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style=style)
    for text, opts in parts:
        r = p.add_run(text)
        for k,v in opts.items():
            if k == 'bold': r.bold=v
            elif k == 'italic': r.italic=v
            elif k == 'color': r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(*v)
            elif k == 'size': r.font.size = Pt(v)
            elif k == 'strike': r.font.strike=v
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(space_after)
    return p

    p = doc.add_paragraph()

# Article I
add_text(doc,'Article I — Definitions','Heading 1')
add_issue(doc,1,'Section 1.01','Material Adverse Effect — disproportionate-impact exceptions','Critical',
'''"Material Adverse Effect" means any event, change, effect, development, state of facts, condition, circumstance, or occurrence that, individually or in the aggregate, has had or would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on (a) the business, assets, liabilities, financial condition, or results of operations of the Company, or (b) the ability of Seller to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement; provided, however, that none of the following, individually or in the aggregate, shall be deemed to constitute, or shall be taken into account in determining whether there has been or would reasonably be expected to be, a Material Adverse Effect: (i) changes in general economic, financial, credit, securities market, or political conditions in the United States or globally; (ii) changes in conditions generally affecting the environmental services industry; (iii) changes in Environmental Laws or regulations; (iv) changes in GAAP or applicable Law (other than Environmental Laws, which are addressed in clause (iii) above); ...''',
'''"Material Adverse Effect" means any event, change, effect, development, state of facts, condition, circumstance, or occurrence that, individually or in the aggregate, has had or would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on (a) the business, assets, liabilities, financial condition, or results of operations of the Company, or (b) the ability of Seller to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement; provided, however, that none of the following, individually or in the aggregate, shall be deemed to constitute, or shall be taken into account in determining whether there has been or would reasonably be expected to be, a Material Adverse Effect: (i) changes in general economic, financial, credit, securities market, or political conditions in the United States or globally; (ii) changes in conditions generally affecting the environmental services industry; (iii) changes in Environmental Laws or regulations; (iv) changes in GAAP or applicable Law (other than Environmental Laws, which are addressed in clause (iii) above); (v) acts of war (whether or not declared), armed hostilities, sabotage, terrorism, military actions, or any escalation or worsening thereof, epidemics, pandemics, earthquakes, hurricanes, tornados, floods, or other natural disasters or acts of God; (vi) the announcement or pendency of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, including any impact on relationships with customers, suppliers, employees, or Governmental Authorities; (vii) any action taken by the Company at the express written request or with the express written consent of Buyer; and (viii) any failure by the Company to meet any internal or external projections, forecasts, or estimates of revenue, earnings, or other financial performance metrics for any period (provided that the underlying facts, circumstances, and causes of any such failure may be considered in determining whether a Material Adverse Effect has occurred); provided, further, that changes, effects, events, or developments described in clauses (i) through (v) shall be taken into account in determining whether a Material Adverse Effect has occurred or would reasonably be expected to occur to the extent such changes, effects, events, or developments disproportionately affect the Company and its Subsidiaries, taken as a whole, relative to other participants in the industries in which the Company and its Subsidiaries operate.''',
'''The industry and regulatory carve-outs are unacceptable without a disproportionate-impact exception. Cascadia is itself an environmental-services business; an industry downturn or regulatory change that affects Cascadia materially more than peers must remain available for the MAE analysis. The proposed language also preserves the existing general carve-outs while preventing them from excluding target-specific CERCLA, RCRA, permitting, or regulatory harm.''',
'''Term Sheet §§7 and 12 (MAE representation and closing condition); Playbook §§2.1–2.2 (mandatory disproportionate-impact qualifier and environmental regulatory exposure); DD Memo §§III, V, and VI (Dalton Creek, permit, and government-contract risks).''')
add_issue(doc,2,'Section 1.01','Indemnification Cap — conform to the term sheet','High',
'''"Indemnification Cap" means Forty-Three Million Dollars ($43,000,000), which is equal to twenty percent (20%) of the Base Enterprise Value.''',
'''"Indemnification Cap" means Twenty-Six Million Eight Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand Dollars ($26,875,000), which is equal to twelve and one-half percent (12.5%) of the Base Enterprise Value.''',
'''The seller draft increases the general cap from the agreed 12.5% to 20% of enterprise value. This is a direct economic deviation, not a drafting judgment. The definition must be corrected and the operative cap in Section 9.04(b) must be conformed.''',
'''Term Sheet §8 (General Indemnification Cap); Playbook §5.1 (cap must match executed term sheet; 12.5% firm target); DD Memo §III (known environmental exposure supports preserving the negotiated cap structure).''')

# Article II
add_text(doc,'Article II — Purchase and Sale; Purchase Price','Heading 1')
add_issue(doc,3,'Section 2.05(d)','Earnout operational covenant — remove affirmative obligations','Critical',
'''From and after the Closing Date through the end of the Earnout Period, Buyer shall, and shall cause the Company to, operate the business of the Company in a manner consistent with past practice and in good faith to maximize the Earnout Payment. Without limiting the foregoing, Buyer shall not, and shall cause the Company not to, take any action that would reasonably be expected to reduce the Adjusted EBITDA of the Company below the levels that would otherwise have been achieved. In furtherance of the foregoing, during the Earnout Period, Buyer shall cause the Company to maintain substantially the same level of personnel, equipment, and other resources as in effect immediately prior to the Closing Date and shall not divert or redirect any contracts, customers, revenues, or business opportunities of the Company to Buyer or any of its Affiliates.''',
'''Following the Closing, Buyer shall not, and shall cause the Company not to, take any action with the primary purpose of reducing or avoiding the Earnout Payment. For the avoidance of doubt, nothing in this Section 2.05(d) shall restrict Buyer\'s right to operate, integrate, restructure, or otherwise manage the Company and its business in Buyer\'s sole discretion, including the right to make capital expenditure decisions, change pricing, make personnel decisions, make strategic investments, acquire or dispose of businesses or assets, allocate corporate resources, restructure the Company or its business, and modify operations, and no such action shall constitute a breach of this Section 2.05(d) unless taken with the primary purpose of reducing or avoiding the Earnout Payment. Buyer shall have no obligation to maintain the Company as a separate entity, maintain any particular level of capital expenditures, retain any particular employees, or refrain from any operational decision, so long as Buyer does not take such action with the primary purpose of reducing or avoiding the Earnout Payment.''',
'''The seller\'s language would constrain integration, restructuring, bolt-on acquisitions, personnel decisions, and resource allocation for the entire earnout period and creates litigation risk over ordinary business judgment. The only acceptable buyer covenant is the narrow primary-purpose negative covenant. Sections 2.05(a)–(c) correctly reflect the $25 million maximum, $38 million full-payment threshold, $32 million floor, linear interpolation, and December 31, 2026 measurement period; no change is needed to those mechanics except to ensure Exhibit D is consistent.''',
'''Term Sheet §5 (earnout economics and negative covenant); Playbook §7.1–7.2 (no affirmative operational obligations; primary-purpose standard); DD Memo §§III–VI (buyer must retain flexibility to manage a platform with environmental projects and government contracts).''')
add_issue(doc,4,'Sections 2.03(d), 2.08(a), and 7.02','Closing debt payoff — payoff letters, funds flow, and closing condition','High',
'''At or promptly following the Closing, Buyer shall cause the Company to repay, discharge, and satisfy in full all Closing Indebtedness. Seller shall use commercially reasonable efforts to cooperate with Buyer in connection with the repayment of such Closing Indebtedness.''',
'''(d) Closing Indebtedness shall be repaid, discharged, and satisfied in full simultaneously with the Closing through the closing funds flow. Seller shall deliver, or cause to be delivered, to Buyer executed payoff letters from each holder of Target Indebtedness no later than three (3) Business Days prior to the Closing Date, including Cascade Mutual Bank with respect to the $28,000,000 senior term loan, Pacific Lease Corp. with respect to the $9,800,000 equipment financing facility, and Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc. with respect to the $4,500,000 subordinated seller note. Each payoff letter shall state the total amount required to repay the applicable obligation in full as of the Closing Date, including principal, accrued and unpaid interest, prepayment premiums, breakage costs, fees, and other amounts required to discharge the obligation; provide wire transfer instructions; and provide for the release of all liens and other security interests upon receipt of the payoff amount, including delivery of applicable UCC termination statements and other lien-release documents. Buyer shall cause the applicable payoff amounts to be paid directly to the applicable holders at the Closing in accordance with the payoff letters and the Funds Flow Agreement. No Target Indebtedness shall remain outstanding after the Closing.''',
'''The seller draft permits repayment after closing and contains no payoff-letter timing, content, or funding mechanics. This is inconsistent with the executed term sheet and the requirements of Clearwater Environmental Lending Corp. Add the above as a pre-closing deliverable and add the following condition to Section 7.02: “Payoff Letters. Seller shall have delivered the payoff letters required by Section 2.03(d) no later than three (3) Business Days prior to the Closing Date, and such payoff letters shall remain in full force and effect as of the Closing.” Add a corresponding seller deliverable in Section 2.08(a) and require the Funds Flow Agreement to include all debt payoffs.''',
'''Term Sheet §6 (three-business-day payoff letters, simultaneous payoff, funds flow, and condition); Playbook §§9.2 and 13.1(f); DD Memo §VI (government contracts and material operating continuity; debt payoff is also required by the buyer lender).''')

# Article IV
add_text(doc,'Article IV — Representations and Warranties Regarding the Company','Heading 1')
add_issue(doc,5,'Section 4.16','Government contracts — change-of-control and novation representations','Critical',
'''(a) The Company is a party to four (4) active government contracts ... with the Oregon Department of Environmental Quality, the Washington Department of Ecology, the United States Army Corps of Engineers, and the Bureau of Land Management (collectively, the “Government Contracts”). (b) Each Government Contract is in full force and effect ... (c) Neither the Company nor any of its directors, officers, or employees is subject to debarment ... (d) The Company has complied in all material respects with all applicable procurement Laws, regulations, and requirements in connection with the Government Contracts.''',
'''Section 4.16 Government Contracts. (a) The Company is a party to the four (4) active Government Contracts listed on Schedule 4.16: the Oregon Department of Environmental Quality contract, the Washington Department of Ecology contract, the United States Army Corps of Engineers contract, and the Bureau of Land Management contract. Seller has delivered to Buyer true, correct, and complete copies of each Government Contract, including all amendments, modifications, task orders, solicitations, and related correspondence. (b) Each Government Contract is in full force and effect and is a legal, valid, and binding obligation of the Company and, to the Knowledge of the Company, the applicable Governmental Authority. Neither the Company nor, to the Knowledge of the Company, any other party is in material breach or default, and no event has occurred that, with notice or lapse of time, would constitute a material breach or default. (c) No Government Contract is subject to a pending or, to the Knowledge of the Company, threatened termination for default or convenience, suspension, non-renewal, material modification, or loss of funding. (d) Neither the Company nor any director, officer, employee, or subcontractor of the Company is subject to debarment, suspension, proposed debarment, proposed suspension, or any exclusion from contracting with any Governmental Authority. (e) The Company has complied in all material respects with all applicable procurement Laws, regulations, and requirements, including the Anti-Assignment Act, 41 U.S.C. § 6305, and applicable FAR Part 42 requirements, and has made all required disclosures and submissions. (f) Except as set forth on Schedule 4.16, no consent, approval, novation agreement, recognition agreement, change-of-name agreement, or other notice is required from any contracting officer or other Governmental Authority as a result of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement; and, to the Knowledge of the Company, no contracting officer has indicated an intent to terminate, suspend, materially modify, or refuse to recognize any Government Contract as a result of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement. (g) Schedule 4.16 identifies, for each Government Contract, any required change-of-control notice, consent, novation agreement, recognition agreement, or other approval and the status of each required submission.''',
'''The existing reps identify the four contracts but do not allocate the specific change-of-control/novation risk. The federal contracts are subject to the Anti-Assignment Act and FAR 42.12; the state contracts require separate review. The revised language requires complete contract copies, status and termination representations, and a schedule of required notices/approvals so that Buyer can measure the risk and enforce the pre- and post-closing covenants.''',
'''Term Sheet §7 (government-contract representations); Playbook §12.2 (government-contract representation, novation covenant, and closing-condition analysis); DD Memo §VI (four active contracts, federal FAR 42.1204 risk, and material revenue/backlog exposure).''')
add_issue(doc,6,'Sections 4.15, 4.16, and 4.17','Environmental sector representations — permit, remediation, and insurance status','High',
'''The Company holds all Environmental Permits necessary for the conduct of its business as currently conducted, and all such Environmental Permits are in full force and effect. ... No Action is pending or, to the Knowledge of the Company, threatened to revoke, suspend, cancel, terminate, modify, or not renew any Environmental Permit. ... The Company maintains environmental impairment liability insurance ... and project-specific environmental liability insurance relating to the Hargrove Industrial Site.''',
'''Add the following sentence at the end of Section 4.15(b): “No Environmental Permit is subject to any pending or, to the Knowledge of the Company, threatened change-of-control notice, approval, transfer, re-issuance, or other regulatory process, except as set forth on Schedule 4.15(b), and Schedule 4.15(b) identifies each such requirement and its status.” Add the following to Section 4.15(f): “All premiums due under each environmental insurance policy have been paid, each such policy is in full force and effect, and no notice of cancellation, non-renewal, rescission, reservation of rights, or material modification has been received.” Add the following sentence at the end of Section 4.16: “The Government Contracts and all related novation, recognition, and change-of-control requirements are accurately described on Schedule 4.16.”''',
'''The draft lists 23 permits and the environmental policies but does not state whether change-of-control notifications/approvals are required or identify their status. The revised language converts the diligence findings into schedule-level representations. Hargrove has approximately $4.2 million of remaining cost and relies on a $10 million site-specific policy; the insurance representation should therefore cover payment status and adverse notices.''',
'''Term Sheet §7 (environmental matters, government contracts, and insurance); Playbook §§3.3, 12.1, and 13.2; DD Memo §§IV, V, VI, and VII (Hargrove, 23 permits, government contracts, and insurance program).''')

# Article VI
add_text(doc,'Article VI — Covenants','Heading 1')
add_issue(doc,7,'Section 6.01(b)','Affiliate transaction restriction during the interim period','High',
'''Without limiting the generality of Section 6.01(a), ... Seller shall not permit the Company to: (i) amend, modify, or restate the articles of incorporation ... (xiii) enter into any non-competition, non-solicitation, exclusive dealing, or similar restrictive covenant agreement.''',
'''Add the following as new Section 6.01(b)(xiv): “enter into any Contract, transaction, or arrangement with, amend, modify, extend, renew, supplement, or terminate any existing Contract, transaction, or arrangement with, or make any payment or transfer any asset to, in each case directly or indirectly, Seller, any Affiliate of Seller, or any officer, director, manager, shareholder, member, partner, or family member of Seller or any Affiliate of Seller, other than compensation payments to employees in the ordinary course of business consistent with past practice, without the prior written consent of Buyer, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed.”''',
'''The draft discloses the $1.6 million annual above-market Affiliate Lease but does not stop Seller from expanding, amending, extending, renewing, prepaying, or adding affiliate arrangements before closing. The covenant should cover both new and existing arrangements and should preserve Buyer consent over value leakage.''',
'''Term Sheet §7 (affiliate arrangements reflected in valuation); Playbook §§3.2 and 3.2 sample covenant; DD Memo §II (above-market affiliate rent adjustment) and §V (permit-dependent operating facilities).''')
add_issue(doc,8,'New Section 6.06','Government-contract novation/recognition and post-closing cooperation covenant','Critical',
'''Section 6.05 Third-Party Consents. Seller shall, and shall cause the Company to, use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain ... all consents, waivers, approvals, authorizations, and notices required ... including those set forth on Schedule 4.05.''',
'''Insert the following as new Section 6.06 and renumber the current Sections 6.06 through 6.11 accordingly: “Government Contracts; Novation and Recognition. (a) From the date of this Agreement until the Closing Date, Seller shall cause the Company to promptly notify each applicable federal and state contracting officer of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement and to prepare and submit all requests, notices, and supporting materials required to obtain any novation agreement, recognition agreement, change-of-name agreement, consent, approval, or other acknowledgement required under the Anti-Assignment Act, 41 U.S.C. § 6305, FAR Part 42, Subpart 42.12, or applicable state procurement Law. (b) Seller and the Company shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain each required novation agreement, recognition agreement, consent, approval, or written confirmation that the applicable process is underway and that the Company may continue interim performance pending completion. Seller shall provide Buyer copies of all submissions and material communications within two (2) Business Days after delivery or receipt and shall not make any material submission or agree to any material modification of a Government Contract without Buyer\'s prior written consent. (c) Seller shall cause the Company to continue performing each Government Contract in compliance with its terms pending completion of the applicable process. (d) Following the Closing, Seller shall reasonably cooperate, at no material cost to Seller, with Buyer and the Company for twelve (12) months, or longer if reasonably necessary to complete a pending process, including by executing documents, providing historical information, and participating in meetings with contracting officers. Seller shall cause its Affiliates to provide the same cooperation.”''',
'''A generic third-party-consent clause is not enough for four material government contracts. The two federal contracts may require novation under FAR 42.1204, and loss of a contract could terminate a material revenue stream. Because agency timing may exceed the Outside Date, the recommended position is mandatory submission, reasonable-best-efforts cooperation, no adverse government signal, and a post-closing tail rather than an absolute requirement that every novation be completed before closing. Discuss with Marcus whether to make receipt of novation/recognition a hard condition for the federal contracts.''',
'''Term Sheet §7 and §12 (government-contract representations and closing conditions); Playbook §12.2 and §13.2(a); DD Memo §VI.C (submit before closing, no denial/termination signal, and post-closing cooperation).''')
add_issue(doc,9,'New Section 6.07','Environmental permits, remediation projects, insurance, and notice covenant','Medium',
'''Section 6.01(a)(iii) requires the Company to maintain “all insurance policies of the Company or replacement policies with comparable coverage on terms no less favorable in the aggregate.” There is no covenant addressing permit-change notifications, post-closing permit cooperation, active remediation, or environmental notices.''',
'''Insert the following as new Section 6.07 and renumber the current Sections 6.06 through 6.11 accordingly: “Environmental Permits and Projects. (a) Prior to the Closing, Seller shall cause the Company to identify each Environmental Permit requiring notification to or approval from an issuing Governmental Authority as a result of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, prepare and submit all required notifications and applications, and provide Buyer copies of each submission and each material response. (b) From the date of this Agreement through the Closing, Seller shall cause the Company to maintain all Environmental Permits and all environmental impairment liability, pollution legal liability, contractor\'s pollution liability, and site-specific environmental insurance policies in full force and effect at coverage levels no less than those in effect on the date hereof; continue the Hargrove Industrial Site remediation in the ordinary course and in compliance with applicable orders, work plans, and Government Contracts; and not voluntarily suspend, terminate, or materially alter any active remediation project without Buyer\'s prior written consent. (c) Seller shall cause the Company to provide Buyer written notice within five (5) Business Days after receipt of any environmental claim, notice of violation, CERCLA § 104(e) or RCRA § 3007 information request, consent order, administrative complaint, or other material regulatory action. (d) For twelve (12) months following the Closing, or longer to the extent reasonably necessary to complete a pending process, Seller shall reasonably cooperate with Buyer and the Company in completing any permit notification, transfer, re-issuance, amendment, or approval process, including by executing documents, providing historical information, and participating in agency communications.”''',
'''The stock structure preserves the permit-holding entity but does not eliminate change-of-control notifications. The covenant addresses the 23-permit portfolio and the four-state regulatory footprint, protects the active Hargrove project and its insurance, and gives Buyer prompt visibility into new environmental claims. The post-closing tail is necessary because agency review may extend beyond closing.''',
'''Term Sheet §7 (environmental matters and insurance); Playbook §§3.3, 12.1, and 13.2(b)–(d); DD Memo §§IV, V, and VII (Hargrove, 23 permits, state notification requirements, and environmental insurance).''')
add_issue(doc,10,'Section 6.09(a) and (b)','Non-competition and non-solicitation — conform to term sheet','Medium',
'''(a) For a period of five (5) years following the Closing Date, Seller shall not ... be connected with any business anywhere in the United States. (b) For a period of three (3) years ... Seller shall not ... solicit, recruit, hire, or engage any employee ... or solicit or encourage any customer, supplier, licensee, licensor, or other business relationship ...''',
'''Replace Section 6.09(a) with: “(a) Non-Competition. For a period of three (3) years following the Closing Date, Seller shall not, and shall cause its controlled Affiliates not to, directly or indirectly, engage in, own, manage, operate, finance, control, or participate in the ownership, management, operation, or control of any business engaged in the provision of environmental remediation services or hazardous waste management services, as such services are conducted by the Company as of the Closing Date, in the States of Oregon, Washington, California, or Nevada; provided that this Section 6.09(a) shall not restrict (i) any portfolio company or operating subsidiary of Seller that is not engaged in environmental remediation or hazardous waste management as of the Closing Date, (ii) Seller\'s existing construction and timber operations, (iii) passive ownership of less than five percent (5%) of the outstanding equity securities of a publicly traded entity, or (iv) environmental-related activities incidental to and performed solely in connection with Seller\'s construction or timber operations.” Replace Section 6.09(b) with: “(b) Non-Solicitation. For a period of two (2) years following the Closing Date, Seller shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to, directly or indirectly, solicit, recruit, hire, or engage any individual who is an employee of the Company as of the Closing Date, or induce, encourage, or attempt to induce or encourage any such employee to terminate employment with the Company; provided that this Section 6.09(b) shall not restrict general solicitations not specifically directed to Company employees or the hiring of an employee who contacts Seller or its Affiliates on the employee\'s own initiative without solicitation.”''',
'''The five-year nationwide “any business” restriction would sweep in Evergreen\'s construction and timber operations and creates enforceability risk. The term sheet specifies a three-year, four-state restriction limited to environmental remediation and hazardous waste management, with express construction/timber carve-outs. The existing three-year employee/customer non-solicit also conflicts with the term sheet\'s two-year employee-only covenant.''',
'''Term Sheet §11 (duration, geography, business scope, bound parties, carve-outs, and two-year non-solicit); Playbook §10.1 (tailored scope and enforceability); DD Memo §II (Company operates in Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada; Seller has unrelated operations).''')

# Article VII
add_text(doc,'Article VII — Conditions to Closing','Heading 1')
add_issue(doc,11,'Section 7.02','Buyer closing conditions — payoff, government-contract status, permits, insurance, and R&W Insurance','Critical',
'''The obligations of Buyer ... shall be subject to ... (a) Representations and Warranties; (b) Covenants; (c) No Material Adverse Effect; (d) Officer\'s Certificate; (e) Seller Deliverables; (f) Third-Party Consents; and (g) Escrow Agreement.''',
'''Add the following new conditions to Section 7.02 and renumber the existing Section 7.02(g) as Section 7.02(k): “(g) Payoff Letters. Seller shall have delivered the payoff letters required by Section 2.03(d) no later than three (3) Business Days prior to the Closing Date, and each payoff letter shall remain effective and provide for release of the applicable liens upon payment. (h) Government Contracts. All required novation, recognition, change-of-name, consent, approval, and change-of-control submissions for the Government Contracts shall have been timely submitted; no applicable Governmental Authority shall have denied such request or notified Seller or the Company of an intent to terminate, suspend, materially modify, or refuse to recognize any Government Contract as a result of the transactions; and, for each Government Contract for which final novation or recognition has not been obtained, the applicable contracting officer shall have provided written confirmation that the process is underway and that interim performance will be permitted. (i) Environmental Permits and Insurance. All notifications required by applicable Law in connection with a change of control of the Company\'s Environmental Permits shall have been submitted, all approvals required before the Closing shall have been obtained, and the environmental insurance policies described in Section 4.15(f) shall be in full force and effect. (j) R&W Insurance. If Buyer elects to obtain a representations and warranties insurance policy, Buyer shall have received evidence reasonably satisfactory to Buyer that the policy has been bound and is in full force and effect.”''',
'''The draft has no debt payoff condition and no separate government-contract or environmental-sector condition. Because full agency novation may take 60–120 days or longer, the buyer-side compromise is to require submission, no adverse agency action, and written permission for interim performance rather than insist on completed novation as an absolute condition. Client decision is required on whether to elevate final novation/recognition to a hard condition for the two federal contracts.''',
'''Term Sheet §§6, 7, and 12 (payoff condition, government-contract conditions, and environmental/insurance representations); Playbook §§9.2, 12.2, 13.1, and 13.2; DD Memo §§V–VII.''')

# Article IX
add_text(doc,'Article IX — Indemnification','Heading 1')
add_issue(doc,12,'Section 9.01','Environmental representation survival — minimum 36 months','High',
'''(b) All representations and warranties contained in this Agreement (other than the Fundamental Representations) shall survive the Closing and continue in full force and effect for a period of twelve (12) months following the Closing Date, and shall thereupon expire and be of no further force or effect.''',
'''Replace Section 9.01 with: “(a) The Fundamental Representations shall survive the Closing and continue in full force and effect until the date that is sixty (60) days following the expiration of the applicable statute of limitations relating to the matters covered thereby, giving effect to any waiver, mitigation, or extension thereof. (b) The Tax Representations shall survive the Closing until sixty (60) days following the expiration of the applicable statute of limitations relating to the matters covered thereby, giving effect to any waiver, mitigation, or extension thereof. (c) The representations and warranties in Sections 4.15 (Environmental Matters), 4.16 (Government Contracts) to the extent relating to environmental or regulatory compliance, and 4.17 (Insurance) to the extent relating to environmental insurance (collectively, the “Environmental Representations”) shall survive the Closing for thirty-six (36) months following the Closing Date. Buyer reserves the right to seek survival of the Environmental Representations through the full applicable statute of limitations, including any period applicable to CERCLA cost-recovery or contribution claims. (d) All other representations and warranties, other than the Fundamental Representations, Tax Representations, and Environmental Representations, shall survive the Closing for eighteen (18) months following the Closing Date. (e) Covenants and agreements that by their terms are to be performed after the Closing shall survive in accordance with their terms; covenants and agreements to be performed before or at the Closing shall survive for twelve (12) months following the Closing Date. (f) No claim may be asserted after the applicable survival period; provided that a claim properly asserted in writing before expiration shall survive until finally resolved.”''',
'''A uniform 12-month survival period is inadequate for environmental liabilities that may take years to crystallize. The minimum buyer position is 36 months, with a preferred full-statute position for CERCLA-related matters. The proposed clause also corrects the draft\'s separate problem that general non-Fundamental representations receive only 12 months, versus the 18-month term-sheet period and the playbook\'s 18–24 month range.''',
'''Term Sheet §8 (18-month general and minimum 36-month environmental survival); Playbook §§4.1–4.2 (environmental minimum and full-statute preference); DD Memo §§III–V (CERCLA latency, active remediation timeline, and permit risk).''')
add_issue(doc,13,'Section 9.02 and new Section 9.09','Dalton Creek Special Indemnity — known CERCLA exposure','High',
'''Section 9.02 lists indemnification for (a) representation breaches, (b) covenant breaches, (c) unpaid Transaction Expenses, and (d) Pre-Closing Taxes.         tcPr.append(shd)

def set_cell_border(cell, **kwargs):
    tc = cell._tc

    tcBorders = tcPr.first_child_found_in('w:tcBorders')
    if tcBorders is None:
        tcBorders = OxmlElement('w:tcBorders')
        tcPr.append(tcBorders)
    for edge in ('top','left','bottom','right','insideH','insideV'):

            tag = 'w:{}'.format(edge)
            element = tcBorders.find(qn(tag))
            if element is None:
                element = OxmlElement(tag)
                tcBorders.append(element)
            for key, value in kwargs[edge].items():
                element.set(qn('w:{}'.format(key)), str(value))
