If Buyer elects to obtain a representations and warranties insurance policy, Buyer shall have received evidence reasonably satisfactory to Buyer that the policy has been bound and is in full force and effect.”''',
'''The draft has no debt payoff condition and no separate government-contract or environmental-sector condition. Because full agency novation may take 60–120 days or longer, the buyer-side compromise is to require submission, no adverse agency action, and written permission for interim performance rather than insist on completed novation as an absolute condition. Client decision is required on whether to elevate final novation/recognition to a hard condition for the two federal contracts.''',
'''Term Sheet §§6, 7, and 12 (payoff condition, government-contract conditions, and environmental/insurance representations); Playbook §§9.2, 12.2, 13.1, and 13.2; DD Memo §§V–VII.''')

'''(a) General Release. On the date that is eighteen (18) months following the Closing Date, the Escrow Agent shall release ... all pending but unresolved indemnification claims ... (b) Final Release. ... amounts shall continue to be held ... until ... thirty-six (36) months following the Closing Date with respect to claims relating to Fundamental Representations. The draft contains no R&W Insurance provision.''',
'''Replace Section 9.08(b) with: “(b) Final Release. With respect to any portion of the Escrow Fund retained as a Pending Claims Reserve, such amounts shall continue to be held until final resolution of the applicable claim or the date that is thirty-six (36) months following the Closing Date, whichever is later, with respect to claims relating to Fundamental Representations, Environmental Representations, or the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity. '''Replace Section 9.01 with: “(a) The Fundamental Representations shall survive the Closing and continue in full force and effect until the date that is sixty (60) days following the expiration of the applicable statute of limitations relating to the matters covered thereby, giving effect to any waiver, mitigation, or extension thereof. '''Insert the following as new Section 6.07 and renumber the current Sections 6.06 through 6.11 accordingly: “Environmental Permits and Projects. (a) Prior to the Closing, Seller shall cause the Company to identify each Environmental Permit requiring notification to or approval from an issuing Governmental Authority as a result of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, prepare and submit all required notifications and applications, and provide Buyer copies of each submission and each material response. (b) From the date of this Agreement through the Closing, Seller shall cause the Company to maintain all Environmental Permits and all environmental impairment liability, pollution legal liability, contractor\'s pollution liability, and site-specific environmental insurance policies in full force and effect at coverage levels no less than those in effect on the date hereof; continue the Hargrove Industrial Site remediation in the ordinary course and in compliance with applicable orders, work plans, and Government Contracts; and not voluntarily suspend, terminate, or materially alter any active remediation project without Buyer\'s prior written consent. (c) Seller shall cause the Company to provide Buyer written notice within five (5) Business Days after receipt of any environmental claim, notice of violation, CERCLA § 104(e) or RCRA § 3007 information request, consent order, administrative complaint, or other material regulatory action. (d) For twelve (12) months following the Closing, or longer to the extent reasonably necessary to complete a pending process, Seller shall reasonably cooperate with Buyer and the Company in completing any permit notification, transfer, re-issuance, amendment, or approval process, including by executing documents, providing historical information, and participating in agency communications.”''',
'''The stock structure preserves the permit-holding entity but does not eliminate change-of-control notifications. The covenant addresses the 23-permit portfolio and the four-state regulatory footprint, protects the active Hargrove project and its insurance, and gives Buyer prompt visibility into new environmental claims. The post-closing tail is necessary because agency review may extend beyond closing.''',
'''Term Sheet §7 (environmental matters and insurance); Playbook §§3.3, 12.1, and 13.2(b)–(d); DD Memo §§IV, V, and VII (Hargrove, 23 permits, state notification requirements, and environmental insurance).''')
add_issue(doc,10,'Section 6.09(a) and (b)','Non-competition and non-solicitation — conform to term sheet','Medium',
'''(a) Non-Competition. For a period of five (5) years following the Closing Date, Seller shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to, directly or indirectly, engage in, own, manage, operate, control, participate in, consult with, render services for, or in any manner be connected with any business anywhere in the United States; provided that the foregoing shall not restrict Seller or its Affiliates from (i) owning, directly or indirectly, solely as a passive investment, securities of any Person that are traded on a national securities exchange if Seller and its Affiliates do not, directly or indirectly, beneficially own five percent (5%) or more of any class of securities of such Person, or (ii) performing its obligations under this Agreement and the other Transaction Documents. (b) Non-Solicitation. For a period of three (3) years following the Closing Date, Seller shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to, directly or indirectly, (i) solicit, recruit, hire, or engage (or attempt to solicit, recruit, hire, or engage) any employee of the Company, or (ii) solicit or encourage (or attempt to solicit or encourage) any customer, supplier, licensee, licensor, or other business relationship of the Company to cease or reduce its business with the Company; provided that the foregoing shall not restrict (A) general solicitations of employment not specifically directed toward employees of the Company, including through advertisements in newspapers, trade journals, or online job boards, or (B) solicitations by headhunters or recruiting firms not specifically directed by Seller or its Affiliates to target employees of the Company.''',
'''Replace Section 6.09(a) with: “(a) Non-Competition. For a period of three (3) years following the Closing Date, Seller shall not, and shall cause its controlled Affiliates not to, directly or indirectly, engage in, own, manage, operate, finance, control, or participate in the ownership, management, operation, or control of any business engaged in the provision of environmental remediation services or hazardous waste management services, as such services are conducted by the Company as of the Closing Date, in the States of Oregon, Washington, California, or Nevada; provided that this Section 6.09(a) shall not restrict (i) any portfolio company or operating subsidiary of Seller that is not engaged in environmental remediation or hazardous waste management as of the Closing Date, (ii) Seller\'s existing construction and timber operations, (iii) passive ownership of less than five percent (5%) of the outstanding equity securities of a publicly traded entity, or (iv) environmental-related activities incidental to and performed solely in connection with Seller\'s construction or timber operations.” Replace Section 6.09(b) with: “(b) Non-Solicitation. For a period of two (2) years following the Closing Date, Seller shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to, directly or indirectly, solicit, recruit, hire, or engage any individual who is an employee of the Company as of the Closing Date, or induce, encourage, or attempt to induce or encourage any such employee to terminate employment with the Company; provided that this Section 6.09(b) shall not restrict general solicitations not specifically directed to Company employees or the hiring of an employee who contacts Seller or its Affiliates on the employee\'s own initiative without solicitation.”''',
'''The five-year nationwide “any business” restriction would sweep in Evergreen\'s construction and timber operations and creates enforceability risk. Add the following sentence at the end of Section 4.16: "The Government Contracts and all related novation, recognition, and change-of-control requirements are accurately described on Schedule 4.16."

**TRACK-CHANGES COMMENT.** The draft lists 23 permits and the environmental policies but does not state whether change-of-control notifications/approvals are required or identify their status. The revised language converts the diligence findings into schedule-level representations. Hargrove has approximately \$4.2 million of remaining cost and relies on a \$10 million site-specific policy; the insurance representation should therefore cover payment status and adverse notices.

**SOURCE CROSS-REFERENCE.** Term Sheet §7 (environmental matters, government contracts, and insurance); Playbook §§3.3, 12.1, and 13.2; DD Memo §§IV, V, VI, and VII (Hargrove, 23 permits, government contracts, and insurance program).
# Article VI --- Covenants
## 7. Section 6.01(b) --- Affiliate transaction restriction during the interim period **\[HIGH\]**
> **SELLER\'S DRAFT --- QUOTED\**

> Section 6.01(b)(xiii): Seller shall not permit the Company to enter into any non-competition, non-solicitation, exclusive dealing, or similar restrictive covenant agreement. The seller draft contains no restriction on entering into, amending, modifying, extending, renewing, supplementing, or terminating any transaction or arrangement with Seller or any Seller Affiliate.
> **BUYER\'S PROPOSED REPLACEMENT --- CLEAN REDLINE TEXT\**

> Add the following as new Section 6.01(b)(xiv): "enter into any Contract, transaction, or arrangement with, amend, modify, extend, renew, supplement, or terminate any existing Contract, transaction, or arrangement with, or make any payment or transfer any asset to, in each case directly or indirectly, Seller, any Affiliate of Seller, or any officer, director, manager, shareholder, member, partner, or family member of Seller or any Affiliate of Seller, other than compensation payments to employees in the ordinary course of business consistent with past practice, without the prior written consent of Buyer, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed."

**TRACK-CHANGES COMMENT.** The draft discloses the \$1.6 million annual above-market Affiliate Lease but does not stop Seller from expanding, amending, extending, renewing, prepaying, or adding affiliate arrangements before closing. The covenant should cover both new and existing arrangements and should preserve Buyer consent over value leakage.

**SOURCE CROSS-REFERENCE.** Term Sheet §7 (affiliate arrangements reflected in valuation); Playbook §§3.2 and 3.2 sample covenant; DD Memo §II (above-market affiliate rent adjustment) and §V (permit-dependent operating facilities).
## 8. New Section 6.06 --- Government-contract novation/recognition and post-closing cooperation covenant **\[CRITICAL\]**
> **SELLER\'S DRAFT --- QUOTED\**

> Section 6.05 Third-Party Consents. Seller shall, and shall cause the Company to, use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain, as promptly as practicable following the date of this Agreement, all consents, waivers, approvals, authorizations, and notices required to be obtained or made in connection with the execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement and the consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby, including those set forth on Schedule 4.05. Buyer shall use commercially reasonable efforts to cooperate with Seller and the Company in connection with obtaining such consents. Notwithstanding the foregoing, neither Seller nor the Company shall be required to pay or commit to pay any amount to (or incur any obligation in favor of) any Person from whom any such consent or waiver may be required (other than filing, application, or similar fees imposed by any Governmental Authority).
> **BUYER\'S PROPOSED REPLACEMENT --- CLEAN REDLINE TEXT\**

> Insert the following as new Section 6.06 and renumber the current Sections 6.06 through 6.11 accordingly: "Government Contracts; Novation and Recognition. (a) From the date of this Agreement until the Closing Date, Seller shall cause the Company to promptly notify each applicable federal and state contracting officer of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement and to prepare and submit all requests, notices, and supporting materials required to obtain any novation agreement, recognition agreement, change-of-name agreement, consent, approval, or other acknowledgement required under the Anti-Assignment Act, 41 U.S.C. § 6305, FAR Part 42, Subpart 42.12, or applicable state procurement Law. (b) Seller and the Company shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain each required novation agreement, recognition agreement, consent, approval, or written confirmation that the applicable process is underway and that the Company may continue interim performance pending completion. Seller shall provide Buyer copies of all submissions and material communications within two (2) Business Days after delivery or receipt and shall not make any material submission or agree to any material modification of a Government Contract without Buyer\'s prior written consent. (c) Seller shall cause the Company to continue performing each Government Contract in compliance with its terms pending completion of the applicable process. (d) Following the Closing, Seller shall reasonably cooperate, at no material cost to Seller, with Buyer and the Company for twelve (12) months, or longer if reasonably necessary to complete a pending process, including by executing documents, providing historical information, and participating in meetings with contracting officers. Seller shall cause its Affiliates to provide the same cooperation."

**TRACK-CHANGES COMMENT.** A generic third-party-consent clause is not enough for four material government contracts. The two federal contracts may require novation under FAR 42.1204, and loss of a contract could terminate a material revenue stream. Because agency timing may exceed the Outside Date, the recommended position is mandatory submission, reasonable-best-efforts cooperation, no adverse government signal, and a post-closing tail rather than an absolute requirement that every novation be completed before closing. Discuss with Marcus whether to make receipt of novation/recognition a hard condition for the federal contracts.

**SOURCE CROSS-REFERENCE.** Term Sheet §7 and §12 (government-contract representations and closing conditions); Playbook §12.2 and §13.2(a); DD Memo §VI.C (submit before closing, no denial/termination signal, and post-closing cooperation).
## 9. New Section 6.07 --- Environmental permits, remediation projects, insurance, and notice covenant **\[MEDIUM\]**
> **SELLER\'S DRAFT --- QUOTED\**

> Section 6.01(a)(iii) requires the Company to maintain "all insurance policies of the Company or replacement policies with comparable coverage on terms no less favorable in the aggregate." There is no covenant addressing permit-change notifications, post-closing permit cooperation, active remediation, or environmental notices.
> **BUYER\'S PROPOSED REPLACEMENT --- CLEAN REDLINE TEXT\**

> Insert the following as new Section 6.07 and renumber the current Sections 6.06 through 6.11 accordingly: "Environmental Permits and Projects. (a) Prior to the Closing, Seller shall cause the Company to identify each Environmental Permit requiring notification to or approval from an issuing Governmental Authority as a result of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, prepare and submit all required notifications and applications, and provide Buyer copies of each submission and each material response. (b) From the date of this Agreement through the Closing, Seller shall cause the Company to maintain all Environmental Permits and all environmental impairment liability, pollution legal liability, contractor\'s pollution liability, and site-specific environmental insurance policies in full force and effect at coverage levels no less than those in effect on the date hereof; continue the Hargrove Industrial Site remediation in the ordinary course and in compliance with applicable orders, work plans, and Government Contracts; and not voluntarily suspend, terminate, or materially alter any active remediation project without Buyer\'s prior written consent. (c) Seller shall cause the Company to provide Buyer written notice within five (5) Business Days after receipt of any environmental claim, notice of violation, CERCLA § 104(e) or RCRA § 3007 information request, consent order, administrative complaint, or other material regulatory action. (d) For twelve (12) months following the Closing, or longer to the extent reasonably necessary to complete a pending process, Seller shall reasonably cooperate with Buyer and the Company in completing any permit notification, transfer, re-issuance, amendment, or approval process, including by executing documents, providing historical information, and participating in agency communications."

**TRACK-CHANGES COMMENT.** The stock structure preserves the permit-holding entity but does not eliminate change-of-control notifications. The covenant addresses the 23-permit portfolio and the four-state regulatory footprint, protects the active Hargrove project and its insurance, and gives Buyer prompt visibility into new environmental claims. The post-closing tail is necessary because agency review may extend beyond closing.

**SOURCE CROSS-REFERENCE.** Term Sheet §7 (environmental matters and insurance); Playbook §§3.3, 12.1, and 13.2(b)--(d); DD Memo §§IV, V, and VII (Hargrove, 23 permits, state notification requirements, and environmental insurance).

'''A uniform 12-month survival period is inadequate for environmental liabilities that may take years to crystallize. The minimum buyer position is 36 months, with a preferred full-statute position for CERCLA-related matters. The proposed clause also corrects the draft\'s separate problem that general non-Fundamental representations receive only 12 months, versus the 18-month term-sheet period and the playbook\'s 18–24 month range.''',
'''Term Sheet §8 (18-month general and minimum 36-month environmental survival); Playbook §§4.1–4.2 (environmental minimum and full-statute preference); DD Memo §§III–V (CERCLA latency, active remediation timeline, and permit risk).''')
add_issue(doc,13,'Section 9.02 and new Section 9.09','Dalton Creek Special Indemnity — known CERCLA exposure','High',
'''Section 9.02 lists indemnification for (a) representation breaches, (b) covenant breaches, (c) unpaid Transaction Expenses, and (d) Pre-Closing Taxes. The draft contains no separate indemnity for Dalton Creek; the only reference is the disclosure of the EPA information request on Schedule 4.19.''',
'''Add the following as new Section 9.02(e): “any Losses arising out of, resulting from, or relating to the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity set forth in Section 9.09.” Insert the following as new Section 9.09: “Dalton Creek Special Indemnity. (a) From and after the Closing, Seller shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Buyer, its Affiliates, the Company, and their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, successors, and assigns from and against any and all Losses arising out of, resulting from, or relating to (i) the pending EPA information request under CERCLA § 104(e) regarding the Company\'s former operations at the Dalton Creek disposal facility located in Clackamas County, Oregon, (ii) any investigation, PRP designation, enforcement action, claim, order, consent decree, administrative order, or proceeding by any Governmental Authority or third party relating to the facility or the Company\'s operations, activities, or waste disposal practices there, and (iii) any contamination, remediation obligation, natural-resource damage, response cost, contribution, defense cost, settlement, or other liability associated with the facility under CERCLA, RCRA, the Oregon Environmental Cleanup Law, or any other applicable Environmental Law. (b) This Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall not be subject to the Basket Amount or the Indemnification Cap, shall be in addition to Seller\'s other indemnification obligations, and Losses recovered under this Section 9.09 shall not reduce the Indemnification Cap or be subject to the Basket Amount. (c) This Section 9.09 shall survive the Closing for seventy-two (72) months. (d) The portion of the Escrow Fund allocated to Dalton Creek Special Indemnity claims shall remain available for such claims for thirty-six (36) months following the Closing Date, less amounts subject to pending and unresolved claims. After that period, Buyer may pursue any remaining or subsequently asserted claim directly against Seller, and Buyer\'s rights shall not be limited to the Escrow Fund.”''',
'''Dalton Creek is a known, material, long-tail liability with an estimated exposure of $1.5 million–$6 million. Treating it only as a scheduled disclosure may eliminate recovery because the matter may not constitute a rep breach and may not mature within the general survival period. The Special Indemnity must be dollar-one, outside the general cap, survive 72 months, and remain supported by escrow for 36 months. Confirm the dedicated-versus-shared escrow allocation with the client; the term sheet requires availability of escrow for the Special Indemnity but does not set a separate dollar amount.''',
'''Term Sheet §9 (Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, 72-month survival, outside basket/cap, 36-month escrow availability); Playbook §6 (known environmental liabilities, dollar-one, 72-month survival, escrow); DD Memo §III (EPA §104(e) request and $1.5 million–$6 million exposure).''')

# Article VII
add_text(doc,'Article VII — Conditions to Closing','Heading 1')
add_issue(doc,11,'Section 7.02','Buyer closing conditions — payoff, government-contract status, permits, insurance, and R&W Insurance','Critical',
'''The obligations of Buyer to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement shall be subject to the satisfaction (or waiver by Buyer) at or prior to the Closing of the following conditions: (a) the Fundamental Representations of Seller shall be true and correct in all respects (other than de minimis inaccuracies) and each other representation and warranty of Seller and the Company shall be true and correct, subject to the Material Adverse Effect standard; (b) Seller shall have performed and complied in all material respects with all covenants and agreements required to be performed or complied with by Seller; (c) since the date of this Agreement, no event, change, effect, development, condition, or occurrence shall have occurred that has had or would reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse Effect; (d) Seller shall have delivered an officer's certificate; (e) Seller shall have delivered all closing deliverables set forth in Section 2.08(a); (f) all consents, waivers, approvals, and authorizations set forth on Schedule 4.05 shall have been obtained and shall be in full force and effect; and (g) the Escrow Agreement shall have been duly executed and delivered by Seller and the Escrow Agent.''',
'''Add the following new conditions to Section 7.02 and renumber the existing Section 7.02(g) as Section 7.02(k): “(g) Payoff Letters. Seller shall have delivered the payoff letters required by Section 2.03(d) no later than three (3) Business Days prior to the Closing Date, and each payoff letter shall remain effective and provide for release of the applicable liens upon payment. (h) Government Contracts. All required novation, recognition, change-of-name, consent, approval, and change-of-control submissions for the Government Contracts shall have been timely submitted; no applicable Governmental Authority shall have denied such request or notified Seller or the Company of an intent to terminate, suspend, materially modify, or refuse to recognize any Government Contract as a result of the transactions; and, for each Government Contract for which final novation or recognition has not been obtained, the applicable contracting officer shall have provided written confirmation that the process is underway and that interim performance will be permitted. (i) Environmental Permits and Insurance. All notifications required by applicable Law in connection with a change of control of the Company\'s Environmental Permits shall have been submitted, all approvals required before the Closing shall have been obtained, and the environmental insurance policies described in Section 4.15(f) shall be in full force and effect. (j) R&W Insurance. If Buyer elects to obtain a representations and warranties insurance policy, Buyer shall have received evidence reasonably satisfactory to Buyer that the policy has been bound and is in full force and effect.”''',
'''The draft has no debt payoff condition and no separate government-contract or environmental-sector condition. Because full agency novation may take 60–120 days or longer, the buyer-side compromise is to require submission, no adverse agency action, and written permission for interim performance rather than insist on completed novation as an absolute condition. Client decision is required on whether to elevate final novation/recognition to a hard condition for the two federal contracts.''',
'''Term Sheet §§6, 7, and 12 (payoff condition, government-contract conditions, and environmental/insurance representations); Playbook §§9.2, 12.2, 13.1, and 13.2; DD Memo §§V–VII.''')
